<meta>This page serves as a celebratory dedication and introductory poem for Jean Léger’s seminal work on the history of the Waldensians. The author, David Stuart, was a professor at Leiden, where Léger lived in exile. The text emphasizes the antiquity and continuity of the Waldensian faith as a precursor to the Reformation.</meta>

->To the Very Reverend and Most Renowned Man,<-

# MR. JEAN LÉGER,

->Formerly a Waldensian Pastor, now a most deserving pastor in Leiden; a congratulation on the publication of the *History of the Waldensians*.<-

<margin>
**a** For 400 years, there have been pastors in his family.
**b** To all the Reformed princes.
**c** Perpetual President of the Synod for 14 years.
**d** He is a "Confessor" <note>One who suffers for the faith without being martyred.</note> because he endured much for Religion.
**e** He himself performed many of the deeds recorded in this History.
**f** No history confirms the permanence of our Religion as much as this one.
**g** He exercised his ministry in Lucerna <note>A reference to the Val Lucerna, one of the Waldensian valleys.</note>.
**h** When the Capitol was being built, all the gods gave way to *Jupiter* except for *Terminus* <note>The god of boundaries</note>, so that it appeared the Roman Empire would have no limits.
**i** The most ancient coat of arms of the Valleys is a torch surrounded by darkness, with this inscription: *The Light shines in the darkness* <note>original: "Lux lucet in tenebris"</note>.
**k** Isaiah 11.
**l** A pyramid stands upon the ruins of his house, with an inscription celebrating him as the "head of the rebellion" because he served as an envoy to the Reformed princes to seek help.
**m** His image was hung in his place <note>An "execution in effigy" where a portrait is hung when the person cannot be captured.</note>.
**n** The Dutch and Walloons are eager to see his portrait hanging in their own homes.
**o** Referring to the new persecutions by the Papists <note>Catholics</note> who stir up various gathered slanders against him.
**p** Indeed, after a solemn investigation was held, the slanders were uncovered, and the imposters were punished.
**q** Namely, that the Waldensians—just like the ancient Christians and the Reformed—suffered similar slanders.
</margin>

> Dear offspring to God, **a** genuine descendant of the Pious:
> *And the solid honor of pure Religion:*
> Pastor, **b** Envoy, **c** President, **d** Confessor, and Exile;
> *To whom no crown is lacking, save that of martyrdom.*
> You suffer what good men must suffer; you do what must be done, and you do it:
> **e** *You do things worth recording; you record pious deeds.*
> Protector of Sacred History, and of the race of the Pious:
> *To whom, through you, their ancient honor shall be restored.*
> For that the Reformed have purely worshipped Jehovah,
> *You clearly teach through the Ancient Religion.*
> **f** With uninterrupted worship and a perennial succession:
> *Which God shall grant to remain thus forever.*
> Pope, why do you insult? Why do you boast of the names of the ancients?
> *Why do you demand we deny our ancient Forefathers?*
> Behold the man who uncovers the false Subalpine arts <note>The deceptive tactics used against the Waldensians in the Piedmont/Alpine region.</note>;
> *With skill, he strips the masked face from you.*
> Rome subdued the Alps after five hundred years;
> *Now, for fifteen hundred years, Rome has been unable to conquer.*
> The boundary-stone of the Italian Region, the bright **g** Lamp;
> *Shall likewise be the boundary of the Italian Religion.*
> **h** Just as Terminus once refused to yield to
> *Tarpeian Jupiter; so may he never yield to him.*
> Blind Pope, do not extinguish the illustrious Lamp;
> *But rather, let the sacred Lamp shine in Rome.*
> May the Sun of Justice be the grandfather-lamp to the Lamp,
> **i** *So that the Light in the darkness may fill Italy.*
> **k** Thus the wolf shall be neighbor to the lamb, and the lamb to the wolf,
> *And the eternal child, Christ, shall rule them both.*
> **l** Let the wicked lies of the Pyramid of Rome be silent,
> *The public path to the Temple shall be one of honor.*
> An unjust sentence of death was passed against a Just man,
> *But God grants him here to enjoy a better life.*
> **m** His likeness suffered the mockery of an infamous death;
> **n** *Yet it shall stand inviolate in countless places.*
> Thus sad things are changed for glad, death for life, darkness for light,
> *Small things for great, and evil for good.*
> Let us marvel at the insane rage **o** of the Divine Fury <note>referring to Erynnis, a Greek Fury/Goddess of vengeance</note>,
> *Which dared to devise dire things against a sacred head.*
> That foulest plague lied of an unspeakable crime:
> *Truly, she is accustomed to gnawing at holy men.*
> Since the fire and sword of the Savoyard could not destroy them,
> *Cunning words are added to savage deeds.*
> How great you are is shown by the rage, anger, and madness of the Herald,
> *Drawn away from the Prince’s arms to the Dutch.*
> While they do the best things, they suffer the very worst.
> **p** A victor and unvanquished, you rise up greater after these things;
> **q** *And two fictional crimes teach us of the Waldensian.*

->DAVID STUART, Minister, Doctor of Sacred Theology & Philosophy<-
->and Professor of the same in the Dutch Academy.<-

# IN HONOR OF

->The Reverend and Most Learned Man,<-

## MR. JEAN LÉGER.

->Most Vigilant Pastor of the Walloon Church of Leiden.<-

The divine rites and the doctrines of the pious Christians, sent down from heaven and preserved through continuous faith; the truth that was nearly crushed through barbarian centuries, and the learned writings that are a terror to the Roman heights—posterity, Léger, will read of these things with you as the witness. Nor shall your work be unknown to the boundless world, wherever it reaches. 

Thus, diverse pursuits are pleasing in your studies. Now you reveal the hidden commands of God, and the learned pulpits ring out for the people. Now you seek out the hidden things, and your voice explains the oracles of the Holy Word like the honeycombs of Hybla <note>Hybla was an ancient Sicilian city famous for its honey; the poet suggests Léger’s teaching is both sweet and nourishing.</note>. 

You record here the rocky Alpine peaks of your fatherland, and through your writings, you honor your fellow *Waldensians*. You show what a soul conscious of what is right can endure, though harassed on all sides, and how much power lies in religion. You show what small hands and the prayers of good men could achieve, when many thousands fall, slain by only a few. 

These things, learned man, you do not wish your descendants to be ignorant of, and you rescue all that had been obscured by the clouds of the past. Even Religion herself, always most pleasing to the great heavens, flourishes joyfully with such a defender. The dreadful **DARKNESS**, now scattered, flees from the night, and the manifest **LIGHT** <note>original: "LUX manifesta"</note> spreads its radiance. 

Truly, it is a joy to have spent these labors for the Divine and to have earned the favor of God. Since the earth is unable to return thanks for so great a gift, and is not sufficient for your praise, may the great Ruler of highest Olympus <note>A poetic reference to God, common in the Neo-Latin style of the 17th century.</note> pay it in full and bring rewards worthy of your merits.

->A. vander GOES, F. F.<- <note>Likely Adriaan van der Goes, a prominent Dutch official or his son; "F.F." often stands for "fieri fecit" (made this) or "filius" (the son).</note>

### Approval of the Walloon Church Synod of the Netherlands.

A report having been made in this Assembly regarding the reading of the 21st Chapter of the proceedings of the previous meeting by those of our fellow ministers who were charged on our behalf to carefully examine everything in the *General History concerning the occurrences of the Evangelical Churches of the Piedmont Valleys*, composed by our very dear Brother, Mr. *Jean Léger*, one of the ministers of the Church in the city of Leiden, insofar as it might touch upon Doctrine; and being clearly assured by them that nothing was found therein that was not perfectly orthodox and in agreement with the Doctrine established among us: therefore, relying on the aforementioned report and judgment, the Assembly has deemed it right that this Chapter be made clear, so as to encourage the aforementioned Author—as it hereby does—to publish such a worthy work. Under the good pleasure and blessing of the Lord, this work shall be most useful for the edification of our Congregations and for a broad confirmation of the antiquity and purity of the true Doctrine, which has been preserved among that good people of the *Valleys* from time immemorial until now, despite the great persecutions stirred up against them on various occasions by the opponents of that same Truth which we profess.

->*Extracted from the records of the Church Assembly of Naarden, held in September 1668.*<-

->And was signed<-
->ANTONIUS HULSIUS, *Moderator*<-
->J. LOUYS GROURSDES, *Secretary*<-

---

### Copies of the Granted Privileges.

By the favor and permission of the Lords of the States of Holland and West Friesland, it is granted to *Jan le Carpentier*, citizen of the city of Leiden, that he may print or have printed, sell, and trade a certain book titled *General History concerning the occurrences of the Evangelical Churches of the Piedmont Valleys, or the Waldensians, divided into two books and compiled by Jean Léger, Minister and Overseer of the same Congregations, etc.* and this for the period and term of fifteen consecutive years: with a Prohibition to all booksellers and printers or anyone else, whoever they may be, from printing or having printed the said book under the pretext of any change, such as alteration of languages, of letters, of arrangement, etc., or any others they might use therein, or even from selling or trading it within our territory if printed elsewhere, upon penalty of forfeiture of the same and a further fine of one thousand guilders, as more fully contained in the said Letter of Privilege, etc. Given in The Hague on July 22, 1669. Signed *Johan de Witt* <note>Johan de Witt was the Grand Pensionary of Holland and one of the most powerful political figures in Europe at the time.</note>, and sealed with the Great Seal of the High and Mighty Lords of the States. By order of the same Lords of the States: *Simon van Beaumont*.

This same favor was also shown to the said Carpentier by my Lords the States-General of the United Netherlands on July 24, 1669, as is more fully stated in their open Letters regarding this, signed *Johan de Witt*, sealed with the Seal of the High and Mighty Lords of the States and signed by their order by *N. Ruysch*.

It is forbidden by the illustrious Republic of Geneva to all booksellers, printers, or other merchants of their territory to print or have printed the said *Chronicle* <term>Tijt-boeck; literally "Time-book," a common 17th-century term for a historical record or chronicle</term> without the consent of the aforementioned *Carpentier* or his associates, or to disguise or alter it in any way, upon penalty of forfeiture and a sum of money, etc. Given in Geneva on April 14, 1669. By order of the Council, signed *du Puy*.

### Approval of the Walloon Church Assembly of the Netherlands.

A report having been made to this Assembly regarding the reading of the 21st Chapter of the proceedings <note>original: "verhandelingen"; refers to the minutes or records of previous church meetings</note> by those of our fellow ministers who were tasked on our behalf to accurately examine everything in the *General Memoir concerning the events of the Evangelical Churches of the Piedmont Valleys*, composed by our very dear Brother, Mr. Johannes Leger, one of the ministers of the Church of the City of Leiden, which might in any way touch upon Doctrine; and being clearly assured by them that nothing has been found therein that was not perfectly orthodox <note>original: "recht-sinnig"; meaning in strict agreement with established religious doctrines</note> and in harmony with the Doctrine confirmed among us: so has this Assembly, trusting in the said report and judgment, deemed it right that this Chapter be made clear, so as to encourage the aforementioned Author—as it also does by these presents—to publish such a worthy work. This work, under the good pleasure and blessing of the Lord, shall be highly useful for the edification of our Congregations and for a broad confirmation of the antiquity and purity of the true Doctrine, which has been preserved among those good People of the Valleys from time immemorial until now, despite the great persecutions stirred up against them on several occasions by the opponents of that same Truth which we profess.

->*Extracted from the records of the Church Assembly of Naarden, held in September 1668.*<-

->And was signed<-
->ANTONIUS HULSIUS, *Chairman*.<-
->J. LOUYS GROURSDES, *Secretary*.<-

Ruysch*.

# DEDICATION.

<meta>catchword: of</meta>

of [their patrons'] praise, making them into the most glorious and eloquent eulogies, striving above all to ingratiate themselves most earnestly into their favor.

As for me, Very High and Mighty Lords, I prefer in this regard, and in approaching **Your Illustrious Mightinesses**, to follow those ancient peoples who never worshipped their gods except with a finger upon their mouths; knowing very well that if Heathendom in former times had such supposed gods who accepted the sacrifices made to them with the flesh and blood of beasts, but nonetheless would by no means tolerate the tongue: **Your Illustrious Mightinesses** are truly those of whom the King after God’s heart <note>referring to King David</note> said in the 82nd Psalm: *You are gods, and you are all children of the Most High*; and who most gloriously occupy the place of His deputies <note>original: "Stede-houders"; here meaning those who hold authority on behalf of God on earth</note> on earth; [and] that you likewise very noble-mindedly reject all the pride of panegyrics <note>elaborate formal praise</note>, as you find your own praise in your wondrous deeds, given to you by the *King of kings and Lord of lords, through whom kings reign and princes decree justice* <note>original: "door welcke de Koningen gebieden ende de Vorstent recht doen"; a reference to Proverbs 8:15</note>. And truly, this [praise] is also such that the pleasure which Divine Omnipotence takes both in **Your Illustrious Mightinesses** yourselves and in your most wise governance, is proclaimed loudly before all the world, demonstrating namely how It <note>Divine Providence</note> is always pouring out its most precious blessings of Heaven, of the Sea, and of the Earth upon you both with full hands; so much so, that you may rightly be said today to be the wonder of angels and men, the comfort of all Orthodox <note>original: "Recht-gelovigh"; referring here specifically to the Reformed or Protestant faith of Europe</note> Europe, and the joy of all your friends and allies, as well as the astonishment and terror...

<summary>In this section of the dedication, Jean Léger explains that he will forgo traditional flowery flattery, arguing that the States-General’s divinely-appointed status and evident worldly success are praise enough.</summary>
<keywords>States-General, Divine Right of Kings, Psalm 82, Protestantism, Dutch Republic, patronage, Jean Léger, religious rhetoric</keywords>

--- Page 26 ---
<meta>This page continues the dedication to the States-General of the United Provinces. The previous page discussed how the author refuses to use empty flattery because the Lords' deeds already prove their greatness. This page begins by dismissing those who might envy the favor shown to the Dutch Republic by God, then explains how the history of the Waldensians is intrinsically linked to the history of the Netherlands and the purity of the Protestant faith.</meta>

# D E D I C A T I O N.

*of all those whose eye is evil, because God and His hand over them is good.* <note>original: "welkers ooge quaet is, om dat Godt ende fijne handt over de ſelve goet is"; a reference to the Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard in Matthew 20:15, suggesting that some may envy the divine favor shown to the Dutch.</note>

But if I myself desired otherwise, nonetheless all that I might possibly bring forward would no more increase the radiance and luster of the glory of **Your Illustrious Mightinesses** <term>U. Doorl. Mogenth.; abbreviation for Uw Doorluchtige Mogendheden, the formal title for the States-General of the Netherlands</term> than a small wax candle would the radiant shining of that beautiful star of the day <note>the sun</note>, which she gives so generously at her full midday. It was printed and sent to *Philip II*, King of Spain, in the year 1562; moreover, having been revised and ratified in 1585 at the Church Assembly of Antwerp, it was dispatched to the Emperor *Maximilian* in the year 1588, after it had been signed by a great number of people of high standing (just as previously, and most notably, those under *Philip II*) and was accompanied by a beautiful and excellent letter. In this letter, they testified that they intended not only to live and die by this holy, truly Evangelical faith, but that more than a hundred thousand were ready to seal it with their own blood; just as many of them afterwards joyfully vied with one another to do. It is also this same Confession that the National Church Assembly of the whole French kingdom, held at *Vitry* in the year 1583, accepted and signed with great joy. # L E T T E R
### AND
### A Very Humble Remonstrance to his
# ROYAL HIGHNESS
### O F
# S A V O Y.

*Royal Highness,*

Truth and Justice are, according to the Heavenly Oracles <note>A formal term for the Holy Scriptures</note> delivered by the King and Prophet David, Isaiah, and Zechariah, two virtues so closely joined and bound to one another that it is impossible ever to properly maintain the one without the other. And truly, it serves primarily to keep this very weighty teaching vividly before the eyes of all Princes, Judges, and Authorities of the earth, which an ancient writer, *Aelian*, <note>Claudius Aelianus (c. 175 – c. 235 AD), a Roman author and teacher of rhetoric whose "Varia Historia" was a popular source of moral anecdotes</note> tells us as truth in his *Histories* regarding the chief Judge of the Egyptians: namely, that he had a large Sapphire hanging from his neck directly over his heart, in which this word *Truth* <note>original: 'Αλήθεια (Alētheia)</note> was very artistically carved, and that he never accepted any petitions, heard any arguments, nor pronounced any sentences, without being adorned with this magnificent representation of his duty. By this means, they wished to bring to his mind how necessary it was that he strive to obtain a solid knowledge of matters before he should undertake to make any pronouncement, much less to put what was pronounced into execution. Undoubtedly, this was also the aim—and perhaps it more fortunately impressed the same sentiment into the souls of those to whom *the Lord our Righteousness* <note>A biblical title for God, often referencing Jeremiah 23:6</note> *has given the sword, being an avenger for punishment to him who does evil*, <note>A reference to Romans 13:4 regarding the authority of the state</note> to exercise justice—that Righteousness has been elegantly depicted for them as a naked Woman, having both her level scales in one hand and her threatening sword in the other. For by this it was shown to them that, just as they would stir the weight of accusations and crimes in vain if they did not practice justice in deed, they would likewise boast in vain of doing right if they had not previously occupied themselves laudably with the careful weighing and sharp investigation of matters.

<summary>In this opening of a formal petition to the Duke of Savoy, Johannes Leger uses classical and biblical examples to argue that a ruler must seek absolute truth before exercising the "sword" of justice. He cites the Egyptian custom of wearing a "Truth" pendant and the iconography of Lady Justice to emphasize that judgment without thorough investigation is hollow.</summary>

<header>L E T T E R.</header>
<meta>catchword: commanded</meta>

But in particular, it can in no way be doubted that God had the same purpose when, under the Old Covenant, having placed the High Priests over His People in the authority of Judges, He commanded them to wear the *Urim* and *Thummim* on the Breastplate of Judgment, where the names of all the tribes of Israel were engraved upon twelve precious stones. For just as *Urim* signified the *Light of Truth*, so also *Thummim* signified the *Integrity of Judgment*; and never was the *Thummim* spoken of before the *Urim* was mentioned, to make it known through this that he <note>Referring to the Judge or High Priest</note> could never put *Integrity of Justice* into practice unless he were first sufficiently enlightened by the *Light of Truth*.

If then, on the contrary, the Holy Leaves <note>A poetic reference to the pages of the Bible</note> likewise curse the one *who punishes the innocent and him who sets the guilty free*; so must a Judge especially, if he wishes to escape such a deadly curse, necessarily exert all his strength to distinguish the innocent from the criminal. Thus, being sufficiently informed regarding the matter and the law, he may always pronounce a righteous Sentence *not from the conscience of another, but from his own* <note>original: "non ex aliena conscientia, sed ex sua"</note>—that is, solely according to his own best knowledge and conscience, and not upon the bare report of others.

Now it is such, Royal Highness, that Your loyal subjects of the Valleys <note>The Waldensian or Vaudois communities living in the alpine valleys of Piedmont</note> have often been very wickedly accused, both before Your Illustrious presence and formerly before that of Your Strict Ancestors of Honorable Memory, concerning two matters: the one, that they are *Heretics*; the other, that they are *criminals* and *Rebels*.

The first is undoubtedly of very great weight, since being *Heretics*, they would simultaneously fall away from the true Faith and the true Evangelical Doctrine, attacking true Religion, and consequently must be regarded as pests to the State and the Church. Whereas, on the contrary, if the situation is otherwise, they must continually be viewed as loyal subjects of the one, and true members of the other. And while the cause of God and that of the eternal Salvation or Damnation of souls hangs in no small measure upon this distinction, surely all Princes, who are true Lieutenants of God on earth, are most highly obligated—for the sake of the salvation of their own souls and the desire they must have for that of their People—to approach this with the most dignified, precise, and earnest investigation they can perform. In this, they should follow nothing but the unique light of the Holy Scriptures, because according to the saying of the Holy Apostle, *Faith comes from hearing the Word of God* <note>A reference to Romans 10:17</note>. This is also why God, in the 17th chapter of Deuteronomy, expressly commanded the Kings of Israel...

### HIS ROYAL HIGHNESS.

<meta>catchword: under-</meta>

...commanded that, as soon as they sat upon the throne of their kingdom, they should diligently write out for themselves a copy <note>The original Dutch *dobbel* refers to the "double" or "duplicate" copy of the Law mentioned in Deuteronomy 17:18.</note> of the Law, and that it should be with them and they should read in it all the days of their lives, so as to learn to fear the Lord their God, and to keep all the words of the Law and the Statutes to perform them. Joshua himself was no sooner elevated to be the head and leader of the people—as we see in the first chapter of his book—than the Lord God commanded him to conduct himself in such a way that the book of the Law should not depart from his mouth, but that he should meditate upon it day and night, so that he might take care to act according to everything written therein; by which means alone, and in no other way, He also promised to bless him and make all his ways prosperous.

This was also very diligently followed and fulfilled by the great King David, who for this reason among others was praised as a man after God's own heart. And even when, in the following centuries, various great corruptions had gradually crept into the Church through the fault especially of the Spiritual Lords <note>The clergy or ecclesiastical authorities of that time.</note> of those days, the good kings Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, Josiah, and the like, in order to oppose them, never wished to blindly follow the judgment of the High Priests or the clergy of their time. Instead, having personally taken close knowledge of the errors and superstitions that had slipped into the Church and divine worship, they applied themselves with a heroic zeal to reform them properly according to the Law of God. And it is so far from the case that these great Princes were ever slandered for interfering in such matters as if they did not concern their office, that it is precisely for this reason that their memory has always been blessed and shall remain so until the end of all ages. Indeed, they are praised in an unusual manner in the Holy Scriptures for this, as is specifically noted of the young Prince Josiah, who immediately after obtaining his crown, having banished all the pleasures of youth from his thoughts, devoted himself entirely with an incomparable passion to restoring the service of the Lord according to His Word.

Constantine the Great, the first Christian Emperor, also did not merely convene the first General Church Council at Nicaea <note>The Council of Nicaea (325 AD), intended to resolve the Arian controversy regarding the nature of Christ.</note> to be able to judge the dispute that the Arians had with the true Christians—accusing them, among other things, of heresy. The Arians at that time boasted (much like those today who follow the traditions of the Pope) that they were the true Universal Church and the greatest multitude, as indeed they then were. But Constantine, moreover, always wished to be present there himself and to preside over the righteous...

<meta>This page continues the argument that historical Christian rulers—specifically Emperors Theodosius, Marcian, and Charlemagne—did not defer blindly to Church councils or the Pope, but personally examined religious doctrine against the standard of Scripture. ->L E T T E R.<-
<meta>catchword: oock</meta>

investigation that he conducted into that matter, according to the infallible and most perfect standard of God’s Holy Word, which alone, as a true touchstone, is capable of distinguishing between upright and evil material. It is also this same path that all Kings, Princes, and Lords—such as the great Emperors *Theodosius*, *Marcian*, and many others—have always held in high esteem when entering into similar circumstances; history records them as so many wonderful examples of high wisdom, justice, and prudence, as well as magnanimity.

How? And did not the famous *Charlemagne* <note>original: "Carolus Magnus"</note> himself, toward the end of the eighth century, convene the Council of Frankfurt in Germany? He did so to have the doctrine examined there with all possible diligence according to the same standard of the Holy Scriptures—the doctrine which the infamous Empress *Irene* <note>original: "Irinea"</note> had established almost throughout all of Greece through her small, conspiring Council of Nicaea regarding the introduction of images into places of prayer and the honor she wished for people to show them. This was done even though she had already drawn the Pope of Rome to her side, and he, to further support her, had even dispatched two church legates to the said assembly. Truly, he [Charlemagne] had that new doctrine very carefully weighed by both the Greeks and the Pope, and finding it contrary to the Holy Oracles of God, he condemned it outright as superstitious and guilty of Idolatry. What is more, beyond the Decrees of that same Church Council (consisting of a very great number of Bishops, including Italians, Germans, French, and those of other nations), he chose to publish under his own name the very learned book that *Claudius*, Archbishop of Turin, had written at that time. He did this so that he might explain the matter even more broadly and show to the world that one should by no means tolerate images in the Houses of God—which are intended for His worship alone—much less do them any homage or speak any prayers before them, under whatever pretext it might be. At the same time, he rebuked *the adoration of the Cross and of ancient relics, the invocation of Saints, pilgrimages, and the supremacy of the Pope or the abuse of his Keys* <note>The "Power of the Keys" refers to the authority claimed by the Pope to admit or exclude people from heaven, based on Matthew 16:19.</note>, always maintaining that he [the Pope] sat upon *St. Peter’s seat no differently than the ancient Pharisees sat upon that of Moses.*

In this manner, then, August Prince, **Your Royal Highness** will also be able—following so many great Kings—to rightly judge and distinguish whether **Your Subjects** of the Valleys <note>The "Valleys" refers to the Waldensian communities in the alpine valleys of Piedmont.</note> must truly be considered *obstinate heretics*. They possess the Confession of Faith which they profess, and the New Testament of our great and only Savior Jesus, who alone is powerful to demand what He will from those whom He calls to the inheritance of glory, which...

If the disastrous fire of the year 1655 <note>Leger refers here to the "Piedmontese Easter," a massacre and scorched-earth campaign against the Waldensians where many archives were destroyed.</note> had not robbed you of all the writings of the previous Church Assemblies, you would still find therein, among others from the year 1646, the fine article by which you requested of me—after much persistence—that I should diligently complete the Histories of Master *Pierre Gilles* <note>original: "Pieter Gilles"</note>, of blessed and holy memory. This encouragement, joined with the natural inclination which I already felt for the task, caused me to double the previous diligence with which I had already carefully begun to research all the reports and notes useful for such a work, and to preserve with singular care all those records of the most remarkable events from time to time; with the intention, however, that I would trace the whole matter somewhat deeper than the aforementioned Master *Gilles*, or even Master *Jean-Paul Perrin* <note>original: "Johannes Paulus Perrin"</note> had ever done. For the former dealt only with some tribulations that our Churches of the Valleys endured, and especially those in the year 1561, without mentioning in the least their Doctrine and Church Discipline, much less their Antiquity and true *Apostolic succession* <term>Apostolic succession: the claim that their church's origins and teachings trace directly back to the original Apostles, rather than being a 12th-century invention</term>. ->B R I E F<-
<meta>catchword: yet (original: noch)</meta>

to finally make known to the world who the *true, original Waldensians* were, who gave the others their name—namely, *the inhabitants of the said Valleys*; just as I have brought forth irrefutable proof of this in an entire chapter specifically, and throughout many other places in my book, as the occasion demands. Furthermore, I wished to irrefragably confirm what their *Doctrine*, as well as their *Morals* and *Discipline*, has always been and still is today, all of this not only through their own writings or those of the adherents of their Faith, but even with those of the Bishops of the Diocese in which they live, set against them from time to time by the inquisitors <note>original: *Geweten-dwingers*, literally "conscience-forcers," a term used for those who compelled religious conformity</note>; and from many other writers, their sworn enemies and bloodiest persecutors. At the same time, through such authenticated and irreproachable testimonies, I sought to refute all those who have sought to smear them with a different Faith and shamelessly bark at their way of life. I had also intended to point out, as if with a finger, their unbroken *Apostolic Succession* <note>original: *Apoſtels-vervolgh*; the Waldensian claim that their church descended directly from the Apostles without interruption</note>, showing thoroughly that in various places in the Valleys, the inhabitants had never adhered to the Papal Traditions, which destroy the principal articles of our Faith, and consequently never had need of any reformation regarding such errors: *as well as the manner in which they were able to preserve that entrusted treasure so carefully until now, throughout such dark <note>original: *luyſters*, likely implying lustreless or gloomy</note> and corrupt centuries.* Finally, it was also my intention *to create a General Memoir, or Brief Account, of all the most remarkable Persecutions which they so voluntarily and courageously underwent in defense of such a Holy Doctrine.*

Thus, in the year 1655, I had already scraped together a great heap of material and tools for this structure, and with great expense and effort had extracted everything that could be found far and wide in any inscriptions, instructions, notes, and necessary foundational documents.

But alas! my very dear Brothers, He <note>Referring to God</note> knows how all was unfortunately lost in the fires of the year 1655, without me being able to save even the slightest bit, except for the original documents of your Charters of Privilege <note>original: *Vergun-brieven*, legal documents granting residency and religious rights</note> from the years 1603 and 1620. This alone seemed likely to rob me, once and for all, of the courage and desire to undertake such a work. Finally, however, having been pleaded with anew and strongly urged by many of those who knew of my intention that I should at last complete it, I renewed and doubled the diligence of my research; and having [found materials] in our neighboring Valleys, such as those of *Cluson* and *Queyras*, where the flames of the Turin Destroyers <note>original: *Thurijnſe Vernielders*; the Ducal troops from Turin who carried out the 1655 massacres</note> had not yet broken through,

...having found some very useful documents, I have resumed my original plan. According to my own judgment—and the opinion of shrewder people than I, to whom I have shown my book—I have sufficiently achieved my purpose. This is true even if it is undoubtedly not as well-executed, as magnificent, or as thoroughly proven as it might have been had I received help. I state this plainly, without fear of contradiction: not a single soul on earth has assisted me in the slightest sense. Regardless, as they say in the *Schools* <note>A reference to Scholastic philosophy: *maius et minus non variant speciem* (more or less does not change the species). Even a less-perfect defense of the truth remains the truth.</note>, the "more or less" does not change the nature of the matter. Therefore, the same truth will shine through clearly enough to powerfully convince my opponents and doom them to eternal silence.

However, if any part remains incomplete, it will undoubtedly be the account of the events in the Valleys since the year 1661, when I departed from there. This applies particularly to the *Devastations* of the years 1663 and 1664 and the period following. But regarding this, I must excuse myself by pointing to you; as you well know, and as many letters still in my possession can fully testify, you were afraid. You feared that *if the Court of Turin had even the slightest inkling that you had assisted in the creation of such a Memoir—since truth breeds hatred—it would inevitably result in your humiliation and cause you to suffer bitterly for it afterward.* For this reason, neither your general Church Assemblies nor any of your Teachers or Overseers in particular ever dared to share the information I requested from them—especially since a degree of peace and rest was granted to you by public letters from Turin. Therefore, I was somewhat forced to publish only what I could gather with great effort and expense from letters written during the chaos of the war or from other sources.

Meanwhile, I am entirely confident that even if some circumstances in those places or elsewhere seem ambiguous, or if certain matters I was unaware of were skipped over, you will nonetheless find your cause asserted so powerfully, clearly, and thoroughly. Furthermore, my very dear Brothers, although it is your own History, I have nevertheless had to dedicate the first part of it to the High and Mighty Lords, my Lords the States General <note>The governing body of the Dutch Republic, which was a major supporter of the Waldensian cause.</note> of these fortunate Netherlands, as I also do, and the other part to the Mighty, Praiseworthy, and Most Excellent Evangelical Cantons <note>The Protestant states of the Swiss Confederacy.</note>: all of it, however, in your name and as a testimony of both your and my gratitude. I have done this without placing any burden upon you, because I was certain that you would take it so much more kindly from me, as these Illustrious Powers have always contributed the most to your restoration and preservation, and will be able to contribute more in the future as occasion arises.

Now it is your duty, very true and well-beloved Brothers, to take diligent care here that you, with the Angel of the Church of Ephesus, never *abandon your first love* <note>A reference to Revelation 2:4.</note>, so that it may never happen to you *that he, who holds the seven stars in his right hand and walks among the golden candlesticks, can ever reproach you for having shamefully fallen away from the same.* Wake up instead to diligently perform the first works of the Holy and Glorious Ancestors, of whom you have the honor to be Successors and Followers. In vain would you boast of being Children of Abraham, even though you yourselves might seem to some extent to keep his faith, if you did not at the same time do all his works.

You also, well-beloved Teachers <note>original: *Leeraers*. Referring here to the pastors or ministers of the Waldensian churches.</note>, my most honorable Brothers, strive in God's name more and more to become so many *Tituses* and *Timothies* <note>original Latin: *Titi* and *Timothei*.</note> in order to be, like them, *blameless as God's stewards, not self-willed, not inclined to anger, not given to wine, no striker, no seeker of filthy lucre; but one who gladly hosts, who loves what is good, moderate, just, holy, chaste, who holds fast to the faithful Word, which is according to the Doctrine; so that he may be powerful both to exhort through sound Doctrine and to refute the objectors; being sound in the Faith, rejecting fables and useless questions.*

Show yourselves in everything examples of good Works, showing not only uncorruptedness in Doctrine, but also dignity and sincerity in all your conduct.

And in order to follow in the footsteps of both Timothy and Titus and to testify,

# L E T T E R.

Although you acknowledge that the office God has honored you with is a distinguished work, and you more and more desire to exert the powers of your minds and the strength of your bodies equally to conduct yourselves worthily in it; *bind together faith and a good conscience, be watchful, sober, honorable, hospitable, modest, not greedy for money, ruling your own houses well, keeping your children in subjection with all gravity. Also, do not have any *novices* among you, *lest they fall into the judgment of the devil. Have a good testimony from everyone. Be workers who are not ashamed, and flee the lusts of youth. Always seek the pure Word; persist in season and out of season; refute, rebuke, and exhort with all longsuffering and teaching. Therefore, most venerable and dear Brothers, let no one among you be found as the Angel of the Church of Laodicea <note>A biblical reference to Revelation 3:14–16, where the "Angel" or messenger of the church is rebuked for being "lukewarm"—neither hot nor cold in their faith.</note> was once found: somewhat lukewarm, or a sleeping sentinel, or a silent dog. Be ready to settle all disputes so as to prevent the believers from having to enter into litigation before those whom the Apostle calls *unjust judges*, who by this means attempt to plunge households into total ruin or a shameful falling away from the Faith.

...World, there is no people living anywhere among whom the holy Office of Teaching <term>Leer-ampt: the professional and spiritual role of the ministry</term> is held in such high esteem, or where the true Teachers of Jesus Christ have risen to such great honor and authority, as among that people alone which God has entrusted to You. For every single one of them always humbly accepts as a certainty that You are wiser in all things than they, and furthermore, they remain fully assured by **Your** good conscience. 

In a word, You are the head that governs the body, and consequently, You cause them all to fix their eyes on **You** alone, as those who wish to fashion themselves entirely after your example—or as the saying goes, to "last their shoes" on yours. They follow You strictly as their Shepherds, or herdsmen, and diligently obey You as their faithful Guides. You must not seek your own honor so much as the honor of Him who has sent **You** as His Ambassadors. Consequently, you must flee all secret plotting, which could in any way hinder the *edification of the people*—that people whom You are bound to carry upon your hearts and shoulders, just as the *Breastplate* and the *Linen Ephod* <note>original: *Borst-lap* and *Linne Lijf-rock*. Léger uses them here as metaphors for the intellectual and moral integrity required of a minister.</note>

That the **Elders**, **Almoners** <term>Aelmoeffeniers: Deacons or those responsible for distributing alms to the poor</term>, and others who hold any office in the Church, should most diligently and holily follow and obey the admonition of the Apostle, described in his letter to *Titus 2:1* and *1 Timothy 3:8*, namely *that they be sober, grave, prudent, patient, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not seekers of filthy lucre* <note>original: "vuyl-gewinfoeckers," referring to dishonest or shameful gain</note>, and that which follows.

All of you then—*Teachers, Elders, Almoners*—watch, one as well as the other, so that your wives and all others over whom you are set as Guardians may, according to the Teaching of the same Apostle, *be honorable, virtuous, not slanderers, vigilant, faithful in all things*, and so forth.

Above all things, maintain the perfect obedience and loyalty which the *Royal Prince* <note>Likely referring to the Duke of Savoy, the sovereign ruler of the Waldensian valleys at the time.</note>, given to you by God, must rightly demand of you, not ceasing to pray from the heart for him and his Commanders. In a word, *just as you have received Christ, so walk in Him.*

Be only faithful unto death and the crown of life shall never be withheld from you.*

And concerning me, dear Brothers, *who though absent in body am constantly with you in spirit*, I shall, in doing so, have cause to rejoice over your good condition and the firmness of your faith; and the other members of our Lord Jesus, who shall hear the glad tidings in this regard, shall thank God for you and always be ready to show and testify their Christian compassion toward you everywhere. But if you, on the contrary, degenerate and deviate from that praiseworthy godliness and that great cloud of faithful witnesses of our Lord Jesus, who have maintained themselves before you in our Valleys <note>Léger is referring specifically to the Waldensian Valleys of the Piedmont, where his people lived for centuries.</note>, you shall become the reproach and slander of Angels and Men.

# PREFACE
## TO THE
# R E A D E R.

### Dear Reader,

I will not detain you with a long warning regarding the small errors that have crept into this printing due to the lack of an experienced typesetter, particularly concerning the use of the French language <note>The author is likely referring to the original French edition of his work, or French citations within this text, which he suggests were difficult for the Dutch typesetters to manage.</note>; for it is enough for me to point those out to you in the attached list of printing errors—specifically those that might disturb the meaning and which you must subsequently correct yourself.

Regarding the art of writing <term>Schrijf-konft: referring here to orthography, spelling, and literary style</term>, I have not bound myself too anxiously to either the old or the new styles, deeming it best to hold a middle course. On one hand, I have removed a good number of letters that are never pronounced; yet I have not wished to write everything exactly as it must be spoken.

Concerning my language: if the harsh flavor of the Alps makes it seem a bit rough, it brings as a counterweight, in such beautiful letters, the Waldensian <term>Waldensian: a member of a medieval Christian movement that preceded the Reformation, originating in the Alpine regions of France and Italy</term> grace, sincerity, and simplicity. This should be sufficient to "pass muster," so to speak, for those who seek to know the truth of matters rather than to stammer out the babbling language of heroic fictions. Indeed, they may add that for an Italian—who for nearly fifty years has constantly written, spoken, and taught in his own tongue—it is quite an achievement to be able to make himself understood so well in French.

Some learned, dignified, and zealous people wanted to persuade me to begin my histories with the Massacre of the year 1655 <note>The "Piedmontese Easter" of 1655, a notorious massacre of Waldensians by the troops of the Duke of Savoy, which sparked international outrage.</note>, claiming that, since it set all of Europe in motion and is recounted very differently by various new and one-sided Roman <note>original: "Roomfche," referring to Roman Catholic writers</note> authors, everyone would be most eager to satisfy themselves regarding that event first; indeed, that there would be not a few who would buy and read this book for that reason alone. But after everything was well-considered, I ultimately remained convinced that it is quite unnecessary to alter or overturn the inherent structure of the description and knowledge of events for that reason. On the contrary, in attempting to bring forth a complete account of the original Waldensians, or inhabitants of the Valleys (for the name Waldensian, which formerly only signified their places of residence, has now changed into that of a fellowship or faith, contrasted with the new Roman one), I was compelled first and foremost to firmly establish what that religion, or Waldensian doctrine, has been at all times, and still is, before I could rightly proceed to the treatment of the persecutions they have suffered. Therefore, I take my beginning from there, drawing them first from the own writings of our Waldensians (as it is fair that

# T O   T H E [R E A D E R]

*...that they themselves may be heard, wherever mention is made of their views and Articles of Faith; and thereafter following through the writings of a great number of their most notorious Opponents, even of the Archbishops of Turin <note>The capital of the Duchy of Savoy, whose leaders frequently persecuted the Waldensians in the nearby valleys.</note>, in whose Diocese they live, and the strictest Inquisitors <term>Geweten-dwingers: literally 'conscience-forcers,' referring to the officials of the Inquisition who sought to compel religious conformity</term> who have ever been set against them, as well as through the formal Narratives that they were required to give to the Roman Court, convincingly demonstrating that they have always been just as we find them in their ancient writings; and that all those who have forced any other views upon them were either ignorant or willfully malicious.*

This being done, I proceed to the production of an uncommon number of all kinds of irrefutable proofs, drawn as before from the very Records of the Waldensians, Bishops, Inquisitors, and Popes; by which I shall make it appear clearer than the Sun that at the very same time the darkness of Heathenism was driven from their lands through the Preaching of St. Paul <note>The Waldensians traditionally claimed their church originated from the apostolic era, specifically through the influence of St. Paul or his immediate followers.</note>, or that of his nearest Successors, they, having accepted such a Holy and truly Evangelical Doctrine, have preserved the same uncorrupted, steadfastly, and without any interval or change, so miraculously until now; without even the tares <note>original: "on-kruyt"</note> of Roman Traditions, or any false Doctrine, or the violence of all the persecutions—which the cunning and madness of their Enemies have stirred up against them—ever being able to stifle this Holy Seed; nor could the red Dragon <note>A biblical reference to Revelation 12, where the dragon pursues the 'woman' (the Church) into the wilderness.</note> with all the floods he vomited after this fruitful Woman, even unto the mountains and the wildernesses of the Alps (whither she had fled as to a place appointed for her by God), ever succeed in smothering her or even in the least preventing her from happily bearing and bringing into the world a countless number of true children of Abraham.

Having now thus handled the Doctrine of the Waldensians, their Antiquity, and their preservation in the Valleys, I pass over to their life, discipline, and customs, always proceeding with proofs in the aforementioned manner.

After this, I come in the second Book to relate the unheard-of persecutions which they have suffered at various times, and most notably the massacre of the year 1655 <note>The 'Piedmontese Easter,' a notorious event where the Duke of Savoy's troops committed mass atrocities against the Waldensian population, sparking international outrage.</note> and its aftermath until the end of this current year, 1668. In which I most highly defend their conduct as lawful and refute all the ruses and disguises by which the adherents of Rome—red from the inhumanities committed by them against those poor Believers—either feign or deny them, or even pretend to give them some appearance of justice.

If, however, any of the Readers should become weary through the long narrative that I give in the first Book of the said Waldensian Doctrine, and would rather pass over immediately to the knowledge of their Antiquity and Apostolic succession, and be instructed regarding their life, customs, and conversation, as well as the terrible torments and miraculous deliverances that have happened to them at all times; yes, even to behold the tangible judgments which Heaven has justly brought upon all their Persecutors: they may simply cast an eye upon the Index of the Chapters of each Book, to have their choice of matters according to their pleasure.

I enrich this work with a pleasing and very accurate Map <term>Landt-teyckeninge: a topographical map or chart</term> of the Valleys and other remarkably fine Plates, especially during the treatment of the aforementioned Massacre, in which you shall find those new and Hellish inventions of punishments and cruelties, which Heathen Inhumanity had never yet been able to pull out from the workshop of Hell. Finally, [I] conclude...

# R E A D E R.

*...I conclude with a short treatise on the miraculous and superhuman punishments that the God of justice and vengeance has exercised against the Destroyers of those miserable Believers, adding as an extra a brief summary of my whole life, which I could not and should not have refused at the request of my Friends.*

As for the usefulness of this work, you will find it in this: that it will henceforth always show you in our Waldensian <term>Waldesche: Referring to the Waldensians, a medieval movement that sought to return to apostolic poverty and biblical teaching, surviving centuries of persecution in the Alpine valleys.</term> Churches the three essential marks <term>ken-teyckenen: identifying signs or characteristics used by theologians to distinguish the true church from false ones.</term> by which the Head and the Finisher of our Faith, our great and only Savior Jesus Christ—in whom we boast to be true Christians—wills that we should make an indispensable distinction between the true and the false Church. You will encounter therein, in the first place, a holy and upright agreement with God’s Word, from which alone the true Faith arises, since "Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the Word of God" <note>The author cites Rom. 1, though this famous passage is found in Romans 10:17.</note>. This is the safest, sole, and universal identification-garment <term>ken-kleet: literally a "recognition-robe," a metaphor for an outward sign that identifies someone's status or belonging.</term> by which the Lord Jesus commanded that the Believers, His Sheep, should be known and conveniently distinguished from the Goats and Unbelievers, as He uses these words regarding this in the Gospel of John: "My sheep hear my voice and follow it, and by no means follow that of a stranger" <note>John 10:27</note>. This is that indispensable touchstone through which we can, without any danger of being deceived, certainly distinguish and separate the genuine metal of the scripture from the counterfeit. For you shall find that they [the Waldensians] have never turned back from that Holy Commandment, but rather have resisted all temptations so often placed before them—on one side through flatteries and promises of great earthly advantages, and on the other through very long-lasting and bloody Persecutions. Standing firm with an unchangeable steadfastness in the language and the usage of the Holy Apostles, they have always persevered and followed their favorable Lord and Teacher, who, as "the way, the truth, and the life," could alone bring and lead them through the way of His truth to eternal life and blessedness. They have continually and diligently turned themselves to Him with the words of Saint Peter: "Alas! Lord, to whom should we go, but to you? It is you who have the words of eternal life" <note>John 6:68</note>. Since you may see for yourself throughout all their Writings, and especially in their most solemn Confessions of Faith—yea, what is more, even in the verified accounts of their deadliest Persecutors—that they never wished to accept any Doctrine other than that of the Holy Scriptures, rejecting all Papal Traditions <term>Pauselicke Overleveringen: doctrines or practices of the Roman Catholic Church not explicitly found in the Bible.</term> that conflict with them; which was the sole and true cause of all the terrible torments and devastations they have suffered and endured at all times.

In addition, you shall also find there the second sign of the true Church, inseparably attached to the first, namely a holy walk and conduct, through which they have always diligently transformed the intellectual knowledge <term>hersse-kennis: literally "brain-knowledge," implying a cold or merely theoretical understanding.</term> of pure Doctrine into a heart-knowledge of a spotless life. Thus they have been able to apply to themselves with holy confidence that comforting promise of our Lord Jesus, which He makes to His true Disciples with these words: "You shall be blessed, not if you know these things, but if you do them" <note>John 13:17</note>. For their Faith has always been so active through love that even their Enemies were forced to give them very glorious testimonies, and subsequently to confess that among them (whom they mockingly nicknamed "the good people") the pure and spotless religion before God and the Father was found, consisting, according to the description of Saint James, in visiting the Orphans and Widows in their afflictions and keeping oneself unspotted from the world <note>James 1:27</note>.

Finally, if you have ever been concerned to know who those faithful disciples of Jesus have always been, whose most glorious field-standard <term>velt-wimpel: a military banner or pennant used to identify a unit on the battlefield.</term> and constant sign...

# TO THE

*recognition-garment <term>ken-kleedingh: an identifying costume or uniform. Here, Léger uses it metaphorically to say that suffering is the "uniform" of a true Christian.</term> must be the Cross, as He Himself makes known in the Gospel of Matthew with these words: "he who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me" <note>Matthew 10:38</note>; in that of St. Mark and Luke: "whoever desires to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross and follow Me" <note>Mark 8:34; Luke 9:23</note>; and finally in the Gospel of John: "they will cast you out of the synagogues; and whoever kills you will think he offers a service to God" <note>John 16:2</note>. Paul followed this later in his last letter to Timothy, chapter 3 verse 12, saying: "all those who seek to live godly lives will suffer persecution." You may satisfy yourself in this, dear Reader, with that which is faithfully described and left behind in the entire second book of this writing. And truly, you will not be able to leaf through it with attention without being forced to openly confess at the same time that for our Waldensians <term>Waldenfen: the pre-Reformation Protestant group living in the high valleys of the Cottian Alps.</term>—both those bounded by the circuit of the Alps and those scattered variously across different regions of Europe—that holy condition has steadfastly taken place and still takes place today, which St. Peter once required in the 4th chapter of his first General Letter to the scattered Believers of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia <note>These were Roman provinces in what is now Turkey, where early Christians lived as a minority.</note>, chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father in the sanctification of the Spirit unto obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ. Consequently, the same comforts can be granted to them which those others enjoy in this sense: "Beloved, do not think it strange concerning the fiery trial among you, which happens to you for testing, as though some strange thing happened to you; but as you partake in the sufferings of Christ, so rejoice, that you may also rejoice and be glad in the revelation of His glory. If you are reproached for the name of Christ, you are blessed; for the spirit of glory and the Spirit of God rests upon you. On their part, He is blasphemed; but on your part, He is glorified. But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or thief, or evildoer, or as one who meddles in other people's affairs. But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in this matter: for it is time for judgment to begin at the House of God" <note>Léger is quoting 1 Peter 4:12-17.</note>.*

*Yes, dear Reader, it is with our Waldensians and in this work that you will be able to behold—certainly and according to the Letter—all the features of the description of the persecuted Believers which we have drawn here from St. Peter. But if they have also lived almost constantly like sheep among Raging Wolves, you shall likewise notice that the all-wise, all-compassionate, and all-powerful Providence has preserved them there with no less wonder than Daniel among the lions, his companions in the midst of the flames <note>A reference to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the fiery furnace (Daniel 3).</note>, Israel in Egypt and Babylon, the Dove of the Song of Solomon in the clefts of the rocks against all attempts of the birds of prey, and the pregnant Woman of the Revelation in the wilderness against all the floods which the red Dragon spewed out against her <note>A reference to Revelation 12, often interpreted by Protestants as the Church fleeing persecution.</note>.*

*And if at times it appeared as if this poor little Church, in view of many of her members, was swallowed up by a spiritual Whale <note>The "spiritual whale" likely represents the Roman Catholic Church or the overarching power of the persecuting state, echoing the story of Jonah.</note> like a Jonah; she was nonetheless always found back on dry land shortly thereafter, much bolder than ever before. If at times she was, like the poor wounded man of the Gospel <note>The man from the parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10).</note>, nothing but a wound from head to toe and entirely out of her own weakness; God always raised up one or another Good Shepherd for her, who bound her up and strengthened her so that the gates of Hell could never prevail against her in any way. *Finally, you will also find here that, if in former times the Ahabs and Jezebels <note>Ahab and Jezebel were biblical rulers of Israel who persecuted the prophet Elijah for his opposition to the state-mandated worship of Baal.</note> attributed the confusion and troubles of Israel to Elijah, because he would not join in their idolatry, but on the contrary powerfully rebuked ignorance and sin; if the Jews made of Christ a Man who had a secret understanding with the Devil, who was an enemy of the Supreme Powers, rebellious, and a friend of scoundrels; if both the Jews and Heathens handled the Holy Apostles in the same way and often tried to kill them as disturbers of the public peace; if the ancient Christians were blamed as the only causes of all kinds of storms, earthquakes, and bad times (indeed, Nero even set Rome on fire himself to blame those miserable innocent sheep for it) and were sewn into animal skins and then slaughtered: you will find here, I say, dear Reader, that they have sought to portray our faithful Waldensians <term>Waldensen: a group of pre-Reformation Christians who lived in the high valleys of the Piedmont Alps, often persecuted as heretics by the Church of Rome.</term> in no less a way, seeking to violate them and paint them as monsters for everyone, blackening them like Moors <note>In this context, "blackening like Moors" refers to the metaphorical practice of demonizing a group's reputation to make them appear subhuman or evil.</note> and charging them with all sorts of crimes; in short, according to the prophecy of their Lord, to speak all manner of evil against them while lying. But praise be to God, who shows you at the same time that the "Hell of Conscience" of their greatest Opponents and Oppressors has forced their own mouths to confess this: that it was but lies, and they were happy thereby. You will indeed become aware there that the Court of Turin, or, to speak better, the Council for Propagating the Faith and Extirpating Heretics <note>Original Latin: "propaganda fide & extirpandis hæreticis". This was a powerful administrative body in Turin dedicated to converting Protestants or removing them from the Duke of Savoy's lands.</note>, especially in these recent times, has left nothing undone of what the heaviest slander, the most cunning hair-splitting, and the most wicked language of lies could invent to smear their Innocence, to disguise their Right, and to proclaim them as Rebels throughout the whole world: but at the same time you shall also touch there so tangibly with your finger the wickedness and craftiness of their false deceptions, that they shall only serve to give you that much more of an aversion to their Inventors and compassion for those good souls.*

*It is also only to achieve this objective and to inform future descendants of all these tricks, that I have had to go somewhat more broadly in the account of all those cunning schemes than I would like, judging that it was entirely my duty to free my dear Fatherland from all slander, since I could accomplish it so easily and so clearly through a bare and true account of matters; the more so, since a certain Guichenon <note>Samuel Guichenon (1607–1664), a prominent French historian and genealogist who wrote in favor of the House of Savoy.</note>, Chronicler of His Most Christian Majesty <note>A title for the King of France.</note> and His Royal Highness of Savoy, has recently made public through the Press a great Memoir regarding this, contained in three thick volumes in Octavo (or in Folio), in which he openly falsifies everything against his own knowledge and conscience, as far as it concerns the right, the innocence, and the whole conduct of the Waldensians, both in general and in particular. And truly he is not ashamed (but who shall find that strange in a denier of the faith, who has strayed from the known truth to sell himself to the advantages of lies?) to use his hired pen to lie about the truth of the Massacre of the year 1655 <note>This refers to the "Piedmontese Easter," a notorious massacre of Waldensian civilians by the troops of the Duke of Savoy, which sparked international outrage.</note>, along with all that he believes might in some way serve for the defense of those Believers, and finally to force upon and sell to the world the greatest cruelty and treachery of their enemies as works of uncommon tolerance and goodness. But this was still the most important thing: that the Edicts <term>Plack-kaerten: official public notices or decrees printed on large sheets and posted in public places.</term> which the aforementioned Council for the Extirpation of Heretics sought to spread everywhere, even to the furthest regions of Europe, both in the year 1655 and thereafter, have given no less dangerous suspicion to all People through their strange and usual disguises.*

->TO THE READER.<-

*...the entire undertaken matter will provide all the greater pleasure because I—whereas the aforementioned Guichenon <note>Samuel Guichenon (1607–1664) was a French historian who wrote a history of the House of Savoy, often presenting a perspective unfavorable to the Waldensians.</note> and other chroniclers, along with the previously mentioned Edicts of Prohibition, merely spout everything at their own discretion without any proof, wanting to be believed simply because it pleases them to say it so, as if (as the proverb says) one must blindly believe a criminal on his word—because I, I say, can boast that I never bring anything of weight to light without solid proof; indeed, I consistently have the opponents of the Waldensians <term>Waldensen: a group of pre-Reformation Christians who lived in the high valleys of the Piedmont Alps, often persecuted as heretics by the Church of Rome.</term> as my guarantors, sureties, and irrefutable witnesses of those things which I aptly bring forward everywhere for their defense.*

Observe then, Beloved Reader, with ease in this work the power of the Truth, the stability of the Church, the steadfastness of the Believers, the cunning, faithlessness, wickedness, and fury of all her Enemies, and at the same time the wonders of the Providence of the Heavenly Father, who is accustomed always to work for the best of His Children. Overlook the imperfections of a book that I have been forced to assemble without anyone’s least help, in the midst of the torments of my spirit due to the downfall of my dear Fatherland <note>The author, Jean Léger, refers to the devastation of the Waldensian valleys in 1655 during a period of intense religious persecution.</note>, my own great loss, the illness of nearly all my children, my constant inconveniences, the unrest caused me by the venomous bites and the godless deceit that the shop of my persecutors has been able to provide, and the subsequent and troublesome obstacles of my Service; and pray for me, who, commending you to God and the word of His grace, heartily grants and wishes you here on earth the enjoyment of all your lawful desires and in Heaven the possession of eternal Salvation, AMEN.

## Further notice to the Reader.

Up to here, gracious Reader, the preceding Prefaces of this Work, and at the same time that ancient Spelling and Art of Writing—usually bypassed in all our manuscripts in their time, but nevertheless, both by my absence and by the excessive regard some still had for antiquity thereabouts, only now finally left behind. And because I was somewhat apprehensive whether this all too noticeable difference might not easily come to awaken such great wonder in Your Honor <note>The Dutch "U. E." stands for "Uwe Edelheid," a formal address meaning Your Honor or Your Excellence.</note> that our wonderful Work itself might even suffer some disadvantage thereby; I found it good to detain Your Honor for a moment in this narrow interval with these few words, so that this passion (thus I call Wonder, in spite of the ancient Philosophers) as soon and as quickly as it might arise, might be somewhat stilled and finally lay down. To say something then, through which Your Honor's thoughts might calm down, I pray with all politeness that Your Honor please observe once how we show ourselves human twice here, if it is otherwise human to commit a mistake. For through those same moved reasons, no few misplacements have generally—shall I say crept in, or openly forced their way in? which not seldom come to darken and take away all sense of the words. But while your polite Righteousness, to ensure silence, forbids me to go further into this, as one who rightly assures that it matters little to her whether the same got in there through the fault of Peter or Paul <note>The original Dutch phrase "Pieter of Pauwels" is an idiom equivalent to "whoever the culprit may be" or "this person or that person."</note>; I shall obey the same with a new prayer, requesting simply that Your Honor please, above all things, diligently correct the same, etc.

### Further Notice to the Reader.

Thus far, kind Reader, the preceding Prefaces of this Work, along with that ancient Spelling and Orthography, which in time has generally passed away in all our manuscripts, but which—due both to my absence and the overly great regard some still had for Antiquity—is only now being completely left behind. And because I was somewhat apprehensive whether this all too noticeable difference might not easily provoke such great wonder in Your Honor that our wonderful Work itself might suffer some disadvantage thereby; I found it good in this narrow interval to detain Your Honor with these few words, so that this passion (for so I call Wonder, in spite of the ancient Philosophers <note>The author refers to "Wonderment" as a "passion of the soul," a common concept in 17th-century Cartesian philosophy.</note>) as soon and as quickly as it might have arisen, might be somewhat stilled and finally settle. To say something, then, by which Your Honor's thoughts might be calmed, I pray with all politeness that Your Honor please observe how we show ourselves human here twice over, if it is otherwise human to make a mistake. For by these same stirred-up reasons, quite a few misplacements have generally crept in, or should I say openly forced their way in? which not infrequently come to obscure and take away all sense of the words. But while your polite Justice, to ensure silence, forbids me to go further into this—rightly asserting that it concerns her little whether these errors came in through the fault of Peter or Paul <note>original: "schult van Pieter of Pauwels." A Dutch idiom meaning it doesn't matter exactly which individual is to blame.</note>—I shall obey her with a new plea, requesting simply that Your Honor please, above all things, carefully correct them, etc.

# General Record

has been continued from century to century—just as they, through the grace of that great God who (according to the promise of their good Savior in *Luke 10*) has given them the power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of Satan and the Anti-Christ, still publicly confess today, without ever being led away from the simplicity that is in *Christ* to follow Roman traditions—[God] has willed to gather and keep them together even from the times of the Apostles. Thus, I would ask the kind reader to please join me right at the beginning in looking carefully at the beautiful and suitable location of that land, which God has set as a stage for so many wonders. According to the prophecy of *St. John in Revelation 12*, He had prepared a safe place of refuge for the *Woman clothed with the Sun* <note>The "Woman clothed with the Sun" is a traditional Protestant interpretation of the Church in its pure form, as described in the Book of Revelation.</note>—that is, the Church, which has put on Christ and has the moon *under her feet*—against the waters of persecution with which the wide mouth of the red Dragon might ever seek to flood her. He did this so that, in His own time, He might make her a very fruitful mother (as we shall see fulfilled hereafter) of a great number of other churches, which would be distributed and spread throughout almost the entire Christian world. And since these Valleys are located within the Principality of *Piedmont*, we shall not improperly begin our work with an account of its location and size.

<margin>From where Piedmont takes its name and where it is situated.</margin>
The Princely land of *Piedmont* derives its name from *Pede-montium* <note>Latin: *Pede-montium*, literally meaning "at the foot of the mountains."</note>, because it is situated at the foot of the Alpine mountains. These mountains separate *Gallia Transalpina* <note>Latin: "Gaul across the Alps," or France.</note>, or *France*—so-called because it lies on the other side of the Alps—from *Italy*. Similarly, *Piedmont* itself, and indeed all of ancient *Lombardy* of which it is a part, is called *Gallia Cisalpina* <note>Latin: "Gaul on this side of the Alps."</note>, as if one were to say *France-on-this-side-of-the-Alps*. These names were given to both regions by the Italians, who, from their perspective, were the only ones who could rightly use them. I mention this in passing because it is necessary for the reader to keep in mind that *Piedmont* and the Valleys we are discussing lie in *Hither-Alpine France* and *Lombardy*. This observation will shed no small light on the knowledge of various places in this history, which will mention the *Lombards* and what occurred regarding the Faith in the aforementioned regions, as these events specifically concern the *Piedmontese Valleys*.

The capital city of this Principality is *Turin*, where the Dukes of *Savoy* have long been accustomed to keep their court and residence. It includes within its borders, on the side of *Provence*, the County of *Nice*. Specifically, it has the Duchy of *Milan* to the East, the land of *Montferrat* and the Republic of *Genoa* [to the East], the Mediterranean Sea to the South, and the Alps to the West. These mountains separate it from the regions of *Provence* and *Dauphiné* in Over-Alpine France, just as they separate it from *Savoy* to the North. It is also conveniently traversed by, among others, four great streams. The first and most remarkable of these is the *Po*, which was very elegantly nicknamed *Cornutus Eridanus* <note>Latin: "Horned Eridanus." In classical poetry, rivers were often depicted as bulls or "horned" to represent their branching power.</note>, the horned *Eridanus*, by the world-famous poet *Virgil* on account of its curved branches. It has its source in Mount *Viso*, considered the highest in all *Europe*, which hides its sky-high peak in the clouds to the south of the Valley of *Lucerna*. In this mountain—according to the testimony of the chronicles—that *Carthaginian* General <note>A reference to Hannibal's crossing of the Alps in 218 BCE.</note> knew so well how to cleave those terrifying and inaccessible stone cliffs by that wonderful masterpiece <note>Legend holds that Hannibal used fire and vinegar to crack the Alpine rocks to clear a path for his army.</note> that he paved a way through them for his army; as did King *Francis I*...

### Concerning the Occurrences of the Waldensian Churches.
