Regarding the Events of the Waldensian Churches.

### Concerning Marriage.

Now concerning Marriage, which is also counted among these <note>referring to the sacraments</note> by those of the Papacy <note>a common historical term used by Protestants to refer to the Roman Catholic Church</note>, they have the following words regarding it in a certain book titled *l'Almanac Spiritual*, or Spiritual Guide <note>literally "Spiritual Weather-interpreter," a title suggesting a guide to discerning the spiritual climate or signs</note>, which we have also faithfully translated here:

> ,, Holy Marriage was immediately instituted by God at the beginning of the world.
> ,, Such that it is a very honorable and glorious thing, when it is entered into
> ,, properly and with all purity. Just as the man, who is the head of the
> ,, woman, is obliged to love her, protect her and honorably maintain her,
> ,, always keeping faith and loyalty to her; so also the woman, who was
> ,, created as a help for the man, must be subject to her husband and honor
> ,, him with obedience in all good things, as God commands, taking care of
> ,, his household, guarding herself not only from the deed, but even from all
> ,, appearance of evil and thus keeping equal faith and loyalty to him.
> ,, Whereby they, both persisting in good according to the Teaching of God,
> ,, applying proper diligence to have an honest living without wronging
> ,, anyone, and well-instructing the children granted them by God in the fear
> ,, and teaching of our Lord, shall lead a life conforming to his
> ,, commands. Meanwhile, although fasting and praying, instructing, teaching,
> ,, and timely admonition are of no small use when it comes to a wedding;
> ,, yet the laying on of hands, the binding with the stole <note>a liturgical vestment; the practice refers to a ritual where the priest wraps the couple's hands with his stole</note> and
> ,, a hundred other whimsies, which are commonly maintained here
> ,, outside of clear Scripture simply as human custom, do not at least belong
> ,, to the essence of Marriage itself, nor are they in any way required for it.

But as for the unlawful degrees of kinship and various other things customary among them in the matter of Marriage, these shall be spoken of later in the section on Church Discipline.

### Concerning the Priesthood.

It follows now that we show here what is found in the aforementioned text *l'Almanac Spiritual* regarding their Teaching on the supposed Sacrament of the Priesthood <note>often referred to as Holy Orders</note> and others, which is so short and concise that it may well be read here alongside the previous proofs and our translation into the primary language <note>The author provides the original Old Occitan/Waldensian dialect alongside his Dutch translation</note>. <columns>2</columns>

Of Order it must be held, that Order is called the power given by God to man to duly administer to the Church the word and the Sacraments. But it is not held by Faith of Scripture, but by custom of the Church of such Sacraments. And the testimonial letters, the anointing of the hands, the giving of the belt, and of the vessel <note>original: "ampola," a small jar or flask for holy oil</note> in the hands, & the other things that are commonly observed concerning this <note>original Old Occitan: "De l'Ordre ſe deo tenir, que Ordre ès appellà puiſſança donà de Dio à l'home per aminiſtrar debitament à la Gleiſa la parola e li Sacrament..."</note>

However, we have nothing but the usage of the Church, which would gladly force the same upon us as a Sacrament outside of the Scriptures. ### Concerning Confirmation, or Baptismal Strengthening.

*Now there is the desire for Chrism <note>original: Creſima</note>, which is at present called the Sacrament of Confirmation, lacking a foundation in Scripture for this: that it should first be consecrated by the Bishop, and made of olive oil and balsam, applied to the baptized person on the forehead in the shape of a cross with these words: I sign you with the sign of the cross and confirm you for the sign of Salvation: In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit <note>original Latin: In Nomine Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus Sancti</note>; which is done with the laying on of hands, and involves wrapping a white garment around the head; what they call the Sacrament of Confirmation is not seen to be ordained by Christ, nor by his Apostles. For Christ, the example for the whole Church, was not confirmed in such a manner in his person, nor did he require for his Baptism anointing in this way, but simple water. Therefore, such a Sacrament is not seen to be a necessity for salvation, through which God is blasphemed, being introduced by diabolical movement, so that the people may be mocked in the Faith of the Church, and more belief given to the solemnity or necessity of the Bishops.*

<column-break/>

Now we must also speak of Confirmation <note>original Dutch: Vormſel</note>, which is currently called the *Sacrament of Confirmation, or Strengthening of Baptism*. It is entirely without any ground in the Holy Scriptures, insofar as it is first consecrated by a Bishop, and is mixed together from olive oil and balsam, and then applied in the form of a cross on the forehead of the baptized with these words: *I mark you with the mark of the Cross and confirm you in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit*; the same being performed with the laying on of hands and the head of the baptized bound with a white cloth. And what they call in this sense the *Sacrament of Confirmation or Strengthening* is not found to have been prescribed either by Christ or by his Apostles. For our Savior, the example of the entire Church, did not wish to be so confirmed or strengthened himself, nor did he ever desire that any Anointing <note>original Dutch: Salving</note> should be used in his Baptism, or anything other than pure water. In such a way that such a Sacrament is in no way found necessary for salvation; but on the contrary, God is blasphemed thereby, as having been invented by a Devilish inspiration, so that the people might be deceived thereby, deprived of the Faith of the Church, and finally also give more credence to the ceremonies and necessity of the Bishops.

### XIII. CHAPTER.

#### Regarding the tenth specimen, concerning their Fasting and Comfort for the Sick, taken from the oft-mentioned writing *The Spiritual Almanac*. <note>original: de l'Almanac Spiritual. This was a foundational text for Waldensian practice and belief.</note>

<margin>
*Now follows the Fasting, which is twofold: spiritual and corporal, which is to abstain from eating. But liberty belongs to the Christian to eat at all times, as all days are suitable for fasting, provided it is not observed superstitiously as a virtue of continence. Note that there are some Fasts which are not to be held, nor praised by the faithful, but rather are to be excommunicated and fled. Such are the Fasts of the Scribes and Pharisees, and those ordained by the Anti-Christ <note>The Waldensians often used this term to refer to the Papacy</note> involving Idolatry. The Fasts of the heretics and superstitious which the charmers, sorcerers, and necromancers observe; and the Fasts dedicated to creatures <note>such as saints</note> and not to the Creator, not founded in the Law of God. Also Fasts disordered in foods, especially more rare, more precious, and delicate; such as sea-creatures, figs, raisins, grapes, almonds, of which the poor are deprived while the rich are gluttonous; thus alms are withdrawn from the poor, to whom, if the rich fasted on lighter and common foods, they could more easily and readily provide for their own families and for the [poor]...*
</margin>

<column-break/>

<margin>
*...concerning Fasting.*
</margin>

Here follows now presently the section on Fasting, which is found to be of two kinds: either spiritual or physical. And just as the spiritual consists of abstaining from sinning, so the physical is nothing else than to abstain from usual food. In this regard, it should be well observed that a Christian has the freedom both to eat at all times and to fast on all days, as long as this fasting is not held superstitiously as a virtue of temperance. Here also careful attention must be paid that there are various kinds of Fasting that must not be held or praised by the Believers, but on the contrary must be loathed and fled. Such were the Fasts of the Scribes and Pharisees, and such are still today all those which are prescribed by the Anti-Christ and taste of Idolatry. To these are added the Fast-days of the Heretics and the Misbelieving, which are even celebrated by the tricksters, the sorcerers, and the practitioners of the black arts; as well as all those instituted in honor of creatures <note>meaning saints or other created beings</note> and not the Creator, as none of them are grounded in Divine Law. But among all these, the chief place is held by that improper Fasting which many observe with the most rare [foods]...

# General Memorial.

*...to the other poor. Since fasting does not consist of avoiding any corporal food as if it were evil or unclean. For all things are clean to those who are clean, and nothing is to be refused which is received with thanksgiving: For it is sanctified by the word of God, and by prayer. All those determined fasts are excommunicated, and not promoted by the faithful. Concerning which things they should not be reproved nor blamed.* <note>original: "à li autres pavres...". <column-break/>

[...the best], most costly and delicious foods, such as sea-fish, figs, blue raisins, and almonds; which food the poor so greatly lack, while the rich overflow with them. Indeed, what is more, the poor are hereby deprived of their alms, whereas others, by fasting with a more common and simple table, could provide for their households at less cost and consequently be more mindful of the poor. Nevertheless, one must not think that fasting consists merely in the bare abstaining from some physical food, as if it were in itself unclean and defiled. *On the contrary, all things are clean to those who are clean, and there is nothing to be rejected of that which is taken with thanksgiving. For it is sanctified by the word of God and by prayer.* <note>The author quotes 1 Timothy 4:4-5 to argue against the Catholic practice of forbidding certain foods (like meat) during Lent.</note> So it is that all those set Fasting-days are abominable and rejected by all believers. Concerning which one never heard of anyone being rebuked or held guilty.

### CHAPTER XIV.

#### Regarding the eleventh Sample of the aforementioned Doctrine, making known their sentiments concerning the Anti-Christ and the reasons for their Separation from the Romish Church.

While this article of Faith <note>original: "Geloof-stuk"</note> is still currently being fiercely debated by both sides, it will undoubtedly be not unpleasant to many to deal with the original text itself alongside our translation, which is found in a certain old manuscript Book of Parchment along with several Church teachings of the *Barbes* <note>The 'Barbes' (meaning 'uncles') were the pastors and itinerant preachers of the Waldensian community.</note>. This Book bears the date of the year 1120, and therefore it was known in the world about fifty years before *Waldo of Lyons* <note>Peter Waldo (c. 1140 – c. 1205), traditionally cited as the founder of the Waldensians; the author here argues the group existed long before him.</note>. See here then the title <note>original: "naam-schrift"</note> that is read at the head of this work regarding the *Anti-Christ*.

*Just as the smoke goes before the fire, and the battle before the victory; so also the temptation of the Anti-Christ goes before the glory:* <note>original: "En ayma lo ſum vay devant lo fuoc, la batailla devant la victoria; en ayma la tentation de l'Anti-Chriſt vay devant la gloria"</note>

->That is:<-

Just as the smoke precedes the fire, and the battle precedes the victory; in exactly the same way does the temptation of the Anti-Christ come before Glory.

---

->Thereupon follow these words:<-

<margin>What the Anti-Christ is.</margin>
The Anti-Christ is a falsehood of eternal damnation, covered with the appearance of the Truth and the Righteousness of Christ and His Bride; opposed to the same way of Truth, of Righteousness, of Faith, of Hope, and of Love, to civil life and to the truth of the Service of the Church; presented by the false Apostles and stubbornly defended by both arms <note>This refers to the "two arms" of power: the ecclesiastical (Church) and the secular (State).</note>: or, the Anti-Christ is a hidden deception concerning the truth of salvation in matters of substance and ministry, or it is a fraudulent opposition to Christ and His Bride, and to every faithful member. And thus, he is not any one specific ordained person <note>original Occitan: "Anti-Chriſt ès falſetà de damnation æterna... Et enaymi, non ès alcuna ſpecial perſona ordenà"</note> <margin>No person by himself.</margin>

The Anti-Christ is a falsehood of eternal damnation, covered with the appearance of the truth and the Righteousness of Christ and his Bride; opposed to the same way of Truth, of Righteousness, of Faith, of Hope and of Love, to civil life and to the truth of the Service of the Church; presented by the false Apostles and stubbornly defended by the power of Church and State. One can otherwise also say that the Anti-Christ is a deception which covers the truth of salvation with substantial and ecclesiastical things: or also that he is a cunning opposition against Christ, and against his Bride, and against every faithful Member. In such a way that he is not a single particular head, or man, in any specific dignity,

### Regarding the Occurrences of the Waldensian Churches.
<sig>T 3</sig>

*...in any grade, office, or ministry, and considering this universally. But falsehood itself, set against the truth, covers and adorns itself with beauty and piety outside the Church of Christ—such as in Name, Offices, Scriptures, and Sacraments, and many other things of a similar nature. Iniquity of this kind, with its major and minor Ministers, and those following the law of an evil and blind heart—such a congregation taken together is called the Anti-Christ, or Babel, or the Fourth Beast <note>A reference to the vision in Daniel 7, often interpreted by reformers as a tyrannical power.</note>, or the Harlot, or the Man of Sin, or the Son of Perdition.* <note>original Occitan: "Anti-Chriſt, o Babylonia, o quarta Beſtia, o Meretrix, o home de peccà, Filli de perdition."</note>

...promoted to any honor, office, or ministry, and viewed in such a general sense; but falsehood itself set against the truth, which covers and adorns itself with beauty and godliness outside the Christian Church, just as there are Christ’s Names, Offices, Scriptures, Sacraments, and various other things of a similar nature. Such iniquity then, with all its great and small Servants, and all those who follow the same with an evil and blind heart; such a gathering, I say, so taken together, is called the *Anti-Christ*, or *Babel*, or the *Fourth Beast*, or the *Harlot*, or the *Man of Sin*, or the *Son of Perdition*.
<margin>His names.</margin>

*His Ministers are called false Prophets, lying Masters, Ministers of darkness, the spirit of error, the Apocalyptic harlot, the mother of fornication, clouds without water, autumn trees dead and twice uprooted, waves of the cruel sea, wandering stars, Balaamites, and Egyptians.*

His Servants bear the names of *false Prophets, Lying-masters, Ministers of darkness, the spirit of error, the Harlot of the Holy Revelation, the Mother of fornication, waterless clouds, dead and twice-uprooted Autumn-trees, waves of the cruel sea, wandering stars, Balaamites, and Egyptians.*
<margin>Regarding his Servants.</margin>

<column-break/>

*He is called Anti-Christ because, covered and adorned under the appearance of Christ, and of the Church, and of his faithful members, he opposes the salvation brought about by Christ and truly administered in the Church of Christ; and shared by the faithful through Faith, Hope, and Love. In what way does he oppose it? Through worldly wisdom, through false Religions, and through feigned goodness, through spiritual power, through secular tyranny, through riches, honors of dignities, through delicacies, and through the delights of the world; in all these ways he opposes it.*

He is called *Anti-Christ* because he is clothed and decorated in the garments of Christ, His Community, and her faithful Members, yet he contradicts the Salvation that has been brought about by our Savior and is truly distributed in the Church of Christ, in which the Faithful become participants through Faith, Hope, and Love. But in what manner does he contradict them? Through worldly wisdom, through false Worship, through a feigned goodness, through spiritual power, through worldly tyranny, through riches, honor, and dignities, through delicacies and the pleasures of this earth; in all these ways he goes against them.
<margin>Why he is called Anti-Christ.</margin>

*Therefore, let it be manifest to everyone that the Anti-Christ can in no way be fulfilled, nor come, unless all these aforementioned things are joined together to create hypocrisy and falsehood—namely, when the Wise of the world, the Religious, the Pharisees, the Ministers, the Doctors, the secular power, and the worldly people are joined together. Then they created the man of sin together with error.*

Wherefore everyone may consider themselves warned that the Anti-Christ can never in any way come, unless all these above-mentioned things are joined together with one another, so as to grow into a perfect hypocrisy and falsehood; namely: the Worldly-wise, the Clergy, the Pharisees, the Church-ministers, the Teachers, the State-governing power, and the common worldly folk.
<margin>When revealed.</margin>

# General Memorial Chronicle.

*...of total error. For in the time of the Apostles, although the Anti-Christ was already conceived, yet being an infant, he lacked the necessary internal and external members. Therefore, he was known, destroyed, and excommunicated more easily as one rustic and coarse; he was made mute, for he lacked rational, sensory, and definitive wisdom <note>The author argues the Anti-Christ system was initially weak because it lacked the "wisdom" of sophisticated theological excuses.</note>, for he lacked false Ministers without truth, and human statutes, and lacked external religious orders. Therefore he had fallen into error and sin, but he had nothing with which he could cover the filth or shame of the errors or sin, as he lacked riches and endowments. He could not lead any Minister for himself, nor multiply, preserve, or defend them; for he lacked secular power or authority, so he could not force or constrain anyone from truth to falsehood. For he lacked words, he could not shake or scandalize anyone by his solemnities. And thus being too tender and weak, he could not prevail in the Church. But growing in his members, that is in the blind and hypocritical Ministers, and those of the world, he himself grew into a full-grown man <note>original: "Baron parfait," literally a perfect man or nobleman.</note> in the fullness of his standing <note>original: "plenetà daità."</note>, that is, when the spiritual and secular leaders and lovers of the world, blind in the Faith, multiplied in the Church with all power, being evil. Wishing to be prayed to and honored in spiritual things, to cover his own majesty, malice, and sins, he abused the names of Saints and Pharisees, to this end, as said above. For it is the greatest iniquity to cover and adorn the iniquity worthy of excommunication, and to want to be that which is not given to man, but belongs to God alone, and to Jesus Christ as Mediator. To take away these...*

<column-break/>

All these together thus make the man of sin and of error. For though the Anti-Christ in the time of the Apostles was already conceived, he still lacked many required members, both external and internal, because he was only just beginning to be born. Nevertheless, he was easy to recognize, to destroy, and to place under the ban <note>Excommunication.</note>, as he was at that time much more dull and coarse. Namely, his mouth was then quickly stopped, as he then had neither knowledge nor reason to excuse himself, to plan anything, or to pronounce judgment. He was not then provided with lying servants; he was deprived of human traditions, and visible hypocrites <note>original: "Schijn-heylige," literally "shining-holy ones."</note> were hard to find. Wherefore, although he had indeed fallen into error and sin, he nevertheless had nothing with which he might cover the filth or shame of his errors or sin, since he possessed no riches or endowments. At that time, he could not yet move any Minister to his service, nor increase, maintain, or defend his own; since, stripped of all worldly capacity and power, he could force no one to pass from the truth to a lie. For lack then of all these and similar things, he could not infect or give offense to anyone through his deceptions, and consequently remaining weak and tender, he could get no footing in the Church. But growing in his members—I mean in his Ministers, the blind, hypocrites, and subjects of the world—he shot up into a full-grown man and full age; I say, when the lovers of the earth, both spiritual and worldly, and those blind in the Faith, multiplied in the Congregation with all their might. And truly, while they were evil, they wished to be prayed to and to be of some standing in spiritual matters; they covered their own arrogance, wickedness, and sins, very cunningly misusing the names of the Saints and Pharisees, as has been said before. Now, it is an extreme wickedness to cover and make beautiful a ban-worthy godlessness, and to wish to exalt oneself primarily through that which God alone and the Savior—

...things belonging to God, fraudulently by robbery, and taking upon himself and his own works [the power] seen to be the greatest wickedness: namely, to regenerate, to pardon sins, to distribute the graces of the Holy Spirit, to create Christ <note>original: "conseitar Christ," referring to the doctrine of Transubstantiation where the priest is said to "make" Christ's body during the Mass.</note>, and other such things. And to cover himself in all these things with a mantle of authority and a form of words, and by these things to deceive the rustic people <note>original: "lo poble rostic," meaning the uneducated or simple commoners.</note>, following the world in those things that are of the world, and to depart from God and from the true Faith, and from the reformation of the Holy Spirit; to depart from true penitence, from perseverance in the good, to depart from Charity, from patience, from poverty, from humility; and what is most wicked of all, to depart from true hope, and to think instead on all evil and on the vain hope of the world. To serve all ministries in these things, to make the people commit idolatry, to serve fraudulently the Idols of all the world under the name of the Saints, and their relics and their ministries; so that the people, erring powerfully from the way of truth, think they serve God and do well; to excommunicate those people with hatred, and with anger, and with malice against the faithful and against those who love the truth, and to commit many homicides. And thus the Apostle speaks the truth: who is the man of complete sin <note>original: "home de peccà compli," referring to the 'Man of Sin' in 2 Thessalonians 2:3.</note>, who exalts himself above all that is called God, and all that is worshipped, and who contradicts all truth, and who sits in the temple of God, that is, in the Church, showing himself as if he were God; and who comes in all seduction to those who perish. And if that wicked one has already come perfectly, he is not to be sought, for he is made old by the permission of God, and he already declines: for his power and authority are diminished, and the Lord Jesus kills this wicked one by the Spirit of his mouth, in many men of good will, and sends a contrary power...

<column-break/>

...the Savior as Mediator can never be granted to [any other] man.
<margin>*That he robs our Savior of the honor due to him.*</margin>
So it is that these things—such as the supposed power of rebirth, of the forgiveness of sins, of the distribution of the gifts of Grace of the Holy Spirit, of the making of Christ, and other such matters—to seize them from God through deceit and violence and to claim them for himself and his own works, can be seen as nothing other than a great madness. But in all this, to wish to cover oneself with the mantle of authority and the beautiful appearance of the Word; to deceive the ignorant masses <note>original: "het domme grauw," a 17th-century Dutch term for the unlearned common people.</note> who follow the world in everything belonging to it; to separate oneself from God, from the true Faith, and from the Restoration of the Holy Spirit; to comfortably distance oneself from true repentance, from the practice of virtues, and from perseverance in the good; to unhappily abandon love, patience, poverty, humility, and—what is worst of all—true hope, in order to ground the same in all evil and in an earthly expectation; to subject oneself to every service of ceremonies belonging thereto; to lead the people to idolatry, so far that they, wrongly departing from the way of truth, believe they are thereby performing a service to God and doing well; and finally, under the name of Saints and ancient relics and their service, to cling to every Idol of the world for one’s own subtle deceit, so that one comes to move the people to hatred and wrath against the lovers of truth and to commit many various murders: all of this, I say, is solely the work of him who, according to the true saying of the Apostle, is the perfect man of sin and exalts himself above all that is called God, or is in any way regarded and honored as God; who, sitting in the Temple of God—that is, His Church—shows himself entirely as a God and has come with every kind of seduction for those who perish. Since he has then truly come, he is no longer to be expected. Indeed, it is so far from that, that by God's permission he has already not only grown old, but even his power and authority have already decreased not a little. For the Lord Jesus himself...

For it is the greatest iniquity to cover and adorn the iniquity worthy of excommunication, and to want to be [that] which is not given to man, but belongs to God alone, and to Jesus Christ as Mediator. To take away these...

These all together make thus the man of sin and of error. For though the Anti-Christ was already conceived in the time of the Apostles, yet he lacked many required members from without and from within, because he was only just about to be born. Nevertheless, he was easily known, destroyed, and put under the ban, as being at that time still much more dull and coarse. Namely, his mouth was then quickly stopped, while he at that time had neither knowledge nor reason to excuse himself, to devise anything, or to pronounce judgment. He was then not yet provided with lying-servants <note>original: "leuge-dienaars"</note>, he was deprived of human Traditions <note>original: "Overleveringen"</note> and the visible hypocrites were far to seek. Therefore, though he had indeed fallen into error and sin, yet he had nothing with which he might cover the filth or shame of his errors or sin, because he possessed no riches or endowments. Then he could not yet move any Minister to his service, nor increase, maintain, or defend his own; since, being stripped of all worldly power and might, he could force no one to pass over from the truth to the lie. For lack then of all these and similar things, he could infect no one through his deceptions or give offense; and consequently, remaining weak and tender there, he could get no foothold in the Church. But growing in his members—I mean in his Ministers, blind ones, hypocrites, and subjects of the world—he has shot up into a full-grown man and full age; I say, when the lovers of the earth, both spiritual and worldly, and those blind in the Faith, multiplied with all their might in the Congregation. And truly, while they were evil, they wished to be prayed to and to be of some regard in spiritual matters, they covered their own authority, wickedness, and sins, very craftily misusing the Saints and Pharisees, as was said here before, to that end. Now it is an extreme wickedness to cover and make beautiful a ban-worthy godlessness, and thereby to wish to exalt oneself primarily [in that] which God alone and the Savior...

# Concerning the Occurrences of the Waldensian Churches.

...to fraudulently take things from God through robbery, and to take upon oneself and one's own works [that which belongs to Him], is seen to be the greatest felony. This includes [the power] to regenerate, to forgive sins, to distribute the graces of the Holy Spirit, to consecrate Christ <note>original: "conseitar Christ"; the text is criticizing the claim that a priest "makes" or "consecrates" Christ in the Eucharist</note>, and other such things. And to cover oneself in all these things with the mantle of authority and with a form of words, and thereby deceive the simple people <note>original: "poble rostic", literally rustic or coarse people</note>; to follow the world in these things that are of the world, and to depart from God, from the true Faith, and from the reformation of the Holy Spirit; to depart from true repentance, from perseverance in good, from Charity, patience, poverty, and humility; and what is worst of all, to depart from true hope, thinking instead on every evil and on the vain hope of the world; to serve all ministries for these [worldly] things, to make the people commit idolatry, and to fraudulently serve the Idols of the whole world under the name of the Saints and their relics and their ministries. Thus, the people, wandering wickedly from the way of truth, think they are serving God and doing good. This causes that people to be filled with hatred, anger, and malice against the faithful and against those who love the truth, and leads to many homicides, just as the Apostle spoke the truth [when he asked]: Who is the man of complete sin, who exalts himself above all that is called God and all that is worshipped, and who is contrary to all truth? He sits in the temple of God, that is, in the Church, showing himself as if he were God; and he comes in all seduction to those who perish. And if that wicked one has already come perfectly, he is not to be sought [in the future], for he has been made by God's permission already old, and he is already in decline: for his power and authority are diminished, and the Lord Jesus is killing this wicked one by the Spirit of his mouth in many men of good will, and has sent a contrary power...

<column-break/>

...the role of the Savior as Mediator can never be granted to [mere] man.

<margin>That he robs our Savior of the honor that belongs to him.</margin>

So it is that these things—such as the claimed power of rebirth, the forgiveness of sins, the distribution of the gifts of Grace from the Holy Spirit, the "making" of Christ <note>A critique of the Catholic doctrine of Transubstantiation, where the priest is said to transform bread into the body of Christ</note> and other similar things—to take these from God by fraud and force and to claim them for oneself and one's own works can appear as nothing other than a great madness. But in all this, to wish to cover oneself with the mantle of authority and the beautiful appearance of the Word; to deceive the ignorant masses, who follow after the world in everything that belongs to it; to separate oneself from God, from the true Faith, and from the Restoration of the Holy Spirit; to stubbornly distance oneself from true repentance, from the practice of virtues, and from perseverance in the good; to unhappily abandon love, patience, poverty, humility and—what is the worst of all—true hope, in order to ground it upon all evil and upon an earthly expectation; to subject oneself to every service of ceremonies belonging thereto; to bring the people to idolatry, so far that they, wickedly departing from the path of truth, think they are doing God a service and doing all things well; and finally, under the name of Saints and Ancient Relics and their service, to cling to every Idol of the world for one's own deceit, such that the people are moved to hatred and wrath against the lovers of the truth and commit many various murders: all this, I say, is solely the work of him who, according to the true saying of the Apostle <note>A reference to 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4 regarding the "Man of Sin"</note>, is the perfect man of sin and exalts himself above all that is called God, or is in any way regarded and honored as God; who, sitting in the Temple of God—that is, His Church—displays himself entirely as a God and has come to those who perish with every kind of deception. Since he has then truly come, he is no longer to be expected [in the future]. Indeed, it is so far from that, that by the permission of God he has now not only become old, but his power and authority have already diminished not a little. For the Lord Jesus himself...

# General Memorial

...[con]trary to himself and to those who love him, and he destroys his own places and possessions, and departs from this City of Babylon <note>original: "Babylonia"; in Waldensian thought, Babylon symbolized the corrupt institutional Church in Rome</note> in which every generation draws the strength of its malice.

### What are the works of the Anti-Christ?

<margin>The primary concern of the Anti-Christ is to banish the truth from the world.</margin>
The first work of the Anti-Christ is to take away the truth and change it into falsehood, error, and heresy. The second work of the Anti-Christ is to cover falsehood with the truth and with errors, and to prove and confirm it through Faith and through virtues; to intermingle falsehood in spiritual matters for the subject people, whether in the Ministers, or the Ministry <note>original: "Menestier," referring to the religious offices or services</note>, or in the whole Church. And these two works contain a perfect and complete malice which no tyrant or powerful man could do from the beginning of the world until the time of the Anti-Christ. But Christ never had such an enemy before this one, who could so pervert the way of truth into falsehood, and falsehood into truth—not just in appearance, but as the one who cultivates both truth and falsehood. Thus, the Holy Mother Church with her true Children is entirely trampled down in her truths, especially in the Ministries of the true Ministers in truth, and of the Offices, and the use of them, and of the Children who participate; she weeps mournfully through the speech and the lament of Jeremiah, saying: In what manner does the city of the Pagan and uncircumcised people sit alone? <note>A reference to Lamentations 1:1, comparing the Church's state to the fall of Jerusalem</note> She has become a widow—that is, stripped of the truth of her Spouse. The Lady of the nations through the subjection of errors and sins; the Princess of the Provinces through the division of the world and those things that are in the world. Weeping and...

<column-break/>

...[him]self begins now, by the spirit of his mouth, to kill that evil one in many people of good will, using an opposing power against him and his followers, thrusting him out of his place and possessions, and finally rooting that City of Babel <note>original: "Babel," another name for the corrupt city/church</note> out to the ground, where everything has been corrupted and taken over by wickedness.

### What actually are the works of the Anti-Christ?

Here, he generally takes care above all else to put the truth aside and change it into falsehood, or errors, or heresy. After this, he exerts all his strength to cover that lie with a glimmer of truth, to prove and confirm untruth through faith and virtues, and thus through his Ministers, as well as the whole Service and all that belongs to the Church, to best mix much falsehood with spiritual things for the slave-like and blind-believing people. Now, just as these two ways of acting contain such complete and perfect malice that from the beginning of the world until the times of the Anti-Christ, no tyrant or power has ever been able to do anything like it; so also our Savior never had any enemy before this who could so turn the way of truth into lies, and conversely turn lies into truth, or subvert and corrupt the confessors of both. Consequently, the holy Mother Church, with her true children, is trodden underfoot, especially regarding the matters required for the true and upright service, by the Ministers themselves and their practice, and finally also regarding her children who all share in this. She has reason to complain very bitterly with the words and laments <note>original: "treur-spreuken"</note> of the Prophet Jeremiah, since one can now use these words of her: *How solitary you have become, O city of heathens and uncircumcised people? She has become a widow;* that is, stripped of the truth of her Bridegroom: *a Mistress of the nations,* because she is subject to errors and sin, and *a Princess of the provinces,* because...

# Concerning the Occurrences of the Waldensian Churches.

*...furthermore, and you will now find all things fulfilled by time: for the Holy Church is trusted and held as a Synagogue. And the Synagogue of the wicked is preached as a Mother who truly believes in the Law. Falsehood is preached as equality <note>original: "eygalexa," meaning fairness or justice</note>, injustice is preached and held for justice, error for Faith, sin for virtue, and lies for truth.*

Q. *What works proceed from these first works?*

A. *These. The first work is that he converts the worship of Latria <note>original: "Latrie"; the highest form of worship reserved for God alone</note>, properly belonging to God alone, to himself and to his own works, to the poor rational and irrational creature, sensible and insensible. Rational, such as men, male or female Saints who have passed from this world, and images of gold, gems, and relics. His deeds are the Sacraments, especially the Sacrament of the Eucharist, which he worships as God and as Jesus Christ; similarly, he worships blessed and consecrated things, and forbids worshiping God alone.*

*The second work of the Anti-Christ is that he removes and takes from Christ the merit of Christ, with all the sufficiency of grace, of justice, of regeneration, of remission of sins, of sanctification, of confirmation, and of spiritual nourishment, and assigns it and attributes it to his own authority, to the form of words, to his own works, and to the Saints and their intercession, and the fire of Purgatory, and draws the people away to these things already mentioned, so that they do not seek those of Christ, nor through Christ:*

<column-break/>

...that the world and its belongings have now fallen to her. Weep then with her and live a little longer, and you will clearly find that all those things are now being fulfilled. For the holy Church is now held for a *Synagogue*, and the *Synagogue* or ecclesiastical assembly-place of the wicked is proclaimed for a Mother of those who submit themselves well to the Law. Yes, there falsehood is currently proclaimed for uprightness, injustice for righteousness, error for faith, and finally the lie for truth.

Q. But what follows now from these first principles?

<margin>
*The 1st work is to forbid that one prays to God alone.*
</margin>
A. These works among others, of which the first consists in this: that he perverts the divine service (<term>Latria</term> <note>the specific worship due only to God</note>) which can only properly belong to the Lord, and forces it upon himself and his works, even upon the miserable creature, both rational and irrational, sensible and insensible. Among others, regarding the rational, we have a firm proof in man himself, in that he commands the worship of Saints, both male and female, who have departed this world, as well as golden Images, vile relics <note>original: "vuyle krenken"</note>, and shrines. This also takes place regarding his works—I mean his alleged Sacraments—and especially in the Holy Sacrament of the Altar, as they call it, because he wants it honored alongside God and our Savior with equal prayers, and with blessed and consecrated things. In short, he forbids calling upon God alone.

<margin>
*The 2nd: to rob our Savior of his merits.*
</margin>
The second work of the Anti-Christ lies in this: that he robs and takes from Christ his Mediator's merits, which include the sufficiency of grace, of righteousness, of rebirth, of forgiveness of sins, of sanctification, of confirmation, and of spiritual nourishment; and attributes them all to his own authority, to a certain prescription of words, to his works, to the Saints and their intercession, and finally to Purgatory. Through which he then also brings a division among the people and transfers them to the aforementioned things, so that they [do not seek] the things...

# General Chronicle

*Christ, but only in the works of their hands, and not through the living Faith in God nor in Jesus Christ, and in the Holy Spirit, but through the will and works of the Anti-Christ. Thus he preaches that all salvation consists in his own works.* <note>original Waldensian: "Chrift: ma folament en las obras de las lors mans..."</note>

<column-break/>

Christ, nor anything through Christ, but everything through the works of their hands; seeking to find and obtain nothing through a living Faith in God, or in our Lord Jesus, or in the Holy Spirit, but everything through the will and the work of the Anti-Christ alone. In such a way that he openly teaches that salvation is to be obtained entirely through works.

---

<margin>The 3rd: attributing everything to a dead Faith.</margin>

*The third work of the Anti-Christ is that he attributes the reformation of the Holy Spirit to an outward dead Faith, and baptizes infants into that Faith, teaching that Baptism and regeneration are attained through it, and offers and gives in that same faith the Orders and the other Sacraments, and founds all of Christendom upon it, which is against the Holy Spirit.* <note>original Waldensian: "La terfa obra de l'Anti-Chrift ès que èl attribuìs la reformation del Sanct Sperit à la Fè morta de fora..."</note>

The third work of the Anti-Christ is such that he attributes the Rebirth <note>original: "Herfchepping," literally a re-creation</note> of the Holy Spirit solely and primarily to outward dead Faith, baptizing Children into the same, as that which according to his Teaching is merely required for Baptism and Regeneration; furthermore, he administers the <term>Priesthood|Referring to the "Orders" or the hierarchical clerical ranks of the church</term> and the other Sacraments upon it—in a word, he grounds and establishes the whole of Christendom upon it; which is entirely offensive to the Holy Spirit.

---

<margin>The 4th: introducing human traditions and ceremonies as heathenish as they are solemn for Divine Service.</margin>

*The fourth work of the Anti-Christ is that which together builds and constructs the whole Religion and holiness of the people in his Mass, and has woven together various Jewish ceremonies, and those of the Gentiles and of the Christians. To which, leading the congregation of the people to hear it, he deprives them of spiritual and sacramental eating, and departs from the true Religion and from the Commandments of God, and withdraws from works of mercy through his offerings, and by such a Mass places the people in vain hope.* <note>original Waldensian: "La quarta obra de l'Anti-Chrift ès laqual enfemp baftic..."</note>

The fourth work of the Anti-Christ is this: namely, that he has known how to place the entire Divine Service and holiness of the people in his wretched Mass-service, having patched the same together from various ceremonies, of which some seem borrowed from the Jews, no fewer from the Heathens, and some from the Christians. By which, detaining the Congregation and the people, he robs them of spiritual and Sacramental nourishment; he comes to separate them from the true Divine Service and divine Commandments, withholding them from works of mercy through his Mass-service, and subsequently thrusting the people into such a vain hope through such a Mass, which will inevitably fail them. <note>The Dutch text uses a clever pun: "die haar onmiffelik fal komen te miffen," suggesting the Mass—called "Misse"—will lead to the people "missing" or failing to find salvation.</note>

---

<margin>The 5th: to pursue outward appearance, Simony, and so forth.</margin>

*The fifth work of the Anti-Christ is that he performs all his works so that he may be seen, and that he may work his insatiable avarice, so that he has all things for sale, and does nothing without simony.* <note>original Waldensian: "La quinta obra de l'Anti-Chrift ès quel fai totas las foas obras que èl fia vift..."</note>

The fifth work of the Anti-Christ lies in this: that he works everything in order to be seen, to follow his insatiable greed for money, to keep all things for sale, and to perform nothing without <term>Simony|The sin of buying or selling sacred things, such as church offices or sacraments</term>.

---

<margin>The 6th: to overlook sins.</margin>

*The sixth work of the Anti-Christ is that he gives place to manifest sins, without Ecclesiastical sentence, and does not excommunicate the unrepentant.* <note>original Waldensian: "La fexta obra de l'Anti-Chrift ès, quel dona luoc à li peccà manifeft..."</note>

The sixth work of the Anti-Christ consists in giving place to public sins without pronouncing the slightest Church sentence against them, or placing the unrepentant under the <term>ban|Excommunication or expulsion from the church community</term>.

---

<margin>The 7th: to misuse worldly authority.</margin>

*The seventh work of the Anti-Christ is that he does not rule nor defend his unity through the Holy Spirit, but through secular power.* <note>original Waldensian: "La fep'ima obra de l'Anti-Chrift ès quel non regis..."</note>

The seventh work of the Anti-Christ is this: to know that he does not govern or defend his unity or concord through

In the first place then, and most notably, he uses an outward confession of the Faith for this purpose: of which the Apostle says in such an instance: *They profess with their mouths that they have known God; but deny him at the same time with their works.*

<margin>2. Through Antiquity and the Multitude.</margin>
After that, he also obscures his iniquity through the length of time <note>meaning "tradition" or "antiquity"</note> and the maintaining of some Learned and Clergy, both of male and female gender, who make vows never to marry, and finally through certain Widows and god-fearing Pious Women. Add to this the innumerable people of whom we read in the Holy Revelation: *and to him was given power over every tribe, tongue and nation, and all who dwell upon the earth shall worship him.*

<margin>3. Through the supposed Spiritual and Apostolic power.</margin>
In the third place, he also misuses the spiritual Authority of the Holy Apostles to hide his wickedness; against which the Apostle nevertheless says somewhere: *we have no power against the truth and there is no power given to us for destruction.*

<margin>4. Through Miracles.</margin>

Sixthly, he also makes use therein of certain words of our Savior, as well as the writings of the Early Fathers and even some decrees of the Church Councils, adhering to them only so far as they do not forbid or condemn his wicked life and pleasures.

Finally, in the ninth place, of no small weight is the honorable and austere life of many of those people, although nonetheless not a few have adopted it through mere hypocrisy, as others have through sincerity. Namely, God's Elect, who both will and do good, being imprisoned by him as if in a Babel, <note>Babel or Babylon is used here as a metaphor for a state of spiritual captivity or confusion.</note> serve there as a rich ornamental gold, with which that wicked Anti-Christ covers his vanity; since he in no way wishes to allow them to dedicate their worship to the only God, or to ground their hope in the only Savior, or to understand the true Faith in any way.

All these things and other similar ones serve the Anti-Christ as a mantle and clothes, with which, adorning his lying wickedness, he achieves exactly this: that he is not cast out as a Heathen, even though he struts about most dishonestly and as a harlot among them. Meanwhile, that a Christian, according to the express command he has received from God, is obliged to separate himself from the Anti-Christ, is clearly proven by the Old and New Testament. For so says the Lord himself by the Prophet *Isaiah* in the 52nd chapter, verses 10, 11: *Depart, depart, go out from there, and touch not the unclean: go out from the midst of her, purify*

*...manifestly the malice of the Antichrist and his perversity, etc. For it is commanded by the Lord to depart from him, both inwardly and without. <margin>The testimony of the Waldensians concerning their separation from the Antichrist.</margin>
*Therefore, we knowing these things—the Lord revealing them through his servants, and this revelation growing according to the Holy Scriptures—and we ourselves being admonished by the Commandments of the Lord, we make a separation from him, both exterior and interior, whom we believe to be the Antichrist; and we have a company, and a unity of good will and of right intention, with a pure and simple purpose to please the Lord and be saved: the Lord helping, and the truth of Christ and of his Bride, as much as our small understanding can sustain. Therefore, we have ordained to note what the causes of our departure are, and also of our congregation, so that if the Lord should grant anyone to have this same truth: they may bear the love of it together with us. And if it pleases anyone to teach us more highly and better, we desire to be taught most humbly, and to do better by him, and to be corrected in our defects. *Be it manifest to all and to each individual, that the cause of our departure has been this: as much for the essential truth of the Faith, as for the interior knowledge of one true God, and unity of essence in three persons, which neither flesh nor blood can give. Upon this, we then separate ourselves outwardly and inwardly from those whom we must rightly accept and hold as the Antichrist; knowing the truth of these matters, just as the Lord himself has revealed to us through his servants, believing this Revelation according to His Holy Word and being urged thereto by the Commandments of the Lord; and we form among ourselves, out of free will and sincere intention, a special union and congregation. Through this, we simply intend—provided the assistance of the Lord and that of the truth of Christ and his Bride—that according to the smallness of our understanding we might please the Lord and finally thus obtain salvation. And so that those to whom it might easily please God to give the knowledge of this same truth might love what they have received along with us; we have, after ripe counsel, also seen fit to set down here the reasons for our separation on the one hand, and for our gathering on the other. At the very least, those who perhaps are not yet sufficiently bound shall find some benefit in this service through the Lord's blessing. On the other hand, if anyone should have received something more and more excellent, we request to be instructed by the same with all the more humility and to learn so much good from him that we might thereby correct our failings. That which follows, then, was the cause of our separation.

# Regarding the Occurrences of the Waldensian Churches.
->X<-

*...above all things, the sanctification and the honoring of Him above all things and above every name: living hope through Christ in God, the regeneration and inner renewal through Faith, Hope, and Charity: the merit of Jesus Christ with all sufficiency of grace and justice: the participation or the communion of all the elect: the remission of sins: holy conversation, and the faithful fulfillment of all the Commandments in the Faith of Christ: true penitence, and final perseverance, and eternal life. These are the Ministerial truths: the external congregation of the Ministers, with the people subject to them, in place and in time, in the truth, through the ministerial acts, in the truth mentioned above, leading, establishing, and preserving by faithful and frequent company; the good Ministers by their sense of Faith and of life, being in custom and obedience, and wakefully performing the practice and usage of the Lord over the flocks. The things which the Ministers are intended to serve to the people are these: The Evangelical Word, and the word of reconciliation, or the law of grace according to the sense or intention of Christ. For he must make known the Evangelical Word: the Sacrament joined to the word certifies its sense and understanding, and confirms the hope in Christ and in the faithful. Ministerial communion in all things through the essential truth. And if there be any other ministerial things, they may all be concluded in what has been said.* <note>The text distinguishes between "Essential Truths" (salvation through Christ) and "Ministerial Truths" (the practical administration of the church, such as preaching and sacraments).</note>

### But of these individual truths, some are necessary essentially for human salvation, some conditionally are contained in XII. articles, in the addition of several words

<column-break/>

...the sanctification and honoring of His great name, which belongs to Him above everything and every name; in the living hope through Christ in God, in the rebirth and inner renewal through Faith, Hope, and Love; in the Merits of our Savior with the sufficiency of grace and righteousness; in a fellowship and society with all the elect, in the forgiveness of sins, in a holy way of life, in a faithful fulfillment of all the Commandments through Faith in Christ, in true Repentance, in perseverance to the end and finally in eternal life. But besides these, the Truth of those things *that in some way belong to the Church service* also comes into consideration here, primarily located in the external gathering of the Church teachers with the people under them, coming together at the designated place and time in sincerity, so that through those Truths relating to the Service, having come to those first-mentioned, the same might be strengthened and preserved for a strong and faithful assembly; and that those faithful Ministers of the Word, through an insight of Faith and Life, being in obedience according to custom, might courageously exercise the customary guidance and discipline of the Lord over the flocks. Their duty in service to the people is primarily located here, namely in explaining the Evangelical Word, the word of reconciliation, or the Law of grace according to Christ's sense and meaning. And just as he must proclaim the Word of the Gospel, so the Word-accompanying Sacrament gives no small certainty to their senses and understanding, since he thereby settles the Hope in our Savior in all believers. Now the service-bound community has all things through the aforementioned essential truth. If there should nevertheless be anything else of that sort, it can be entirely included in what has been said.

# General Memorial
<note>Header original: "Algemeyn Gedenk-schrift"</note>

<note>The left column contains a text in an old Romance dialect (Waldensian Occitan) which is then translated or paraphrased in Dutch in the right column. Both have been translated here into English.</note>

...the words <note>original: "rolas"</note> of the Apostles. For the Antichrist is, by Divine permission, already reigning in the Church.

<margin>Summary of the errors and filth of the Antichrist.</margin>
The errors and the uncleannesses <note>original: "non munditias"</note> forbidden by the Lord concerning the Antichrist are these: various and innumerable idolatry against the Commandment of God and of Christ, given to the creature and not to the Creator—whether visible or invisible, bodily or spiritual, intellectual or sensible, natural or manufactured by any art—under whatever name of Christ, or of the holy men, or of the holy women, or of the Relics, or of the authorities. To these creatures, service is rendered through Faith, pilgrimages, alms, offerings, and sacrifices of great expense. These creatures they worship, adore, and honor in several ways: through songs, prefaces, and through the solemnizations and celebrations of Masses, of Vespers, and of Complines <note>the final church service of the day</note> for themselves; through hours, vigils, and festivities, for the acquisition of grace. Yet grace exists essentially in God alone, and meritoriously in Jesus Christ, and is acquired by Faith alone through the Holy Spirit. For there is no other cause of Idolatry than a false opinion of grace, of truth, of authority, of invocation, and of intercession; which the Antichrist himself divides from God and attributes to the ministries and to the works of his hands, to the Saints, and to Purgatory. And this iniquity of the Antichrist is directly against the first article of the Faith, and against the first Commandment of the Law. Similarly, the disordered love of the world and of the Antichrist is the root from which spring all the evils and sins in the Church, from the guides, the rulers, and the officials: who...

<margin>1. Idolatries and Superstition of various kinds.</margin>
<margin>Its first cause.</margin>
<margin>Its second.</margin>

<column-break/>

...words <note>Continuing the sentence from the previous page</note> are contained in the XII principal articles of the Christian Faith, which are but a compilation of various sayings of the Cross-messengers, or Apostles.

Meanwhile, just as the Antichrist, through God's permission, has already ruled in his Church before this time, so he has always held these errors and these filthinesses; namely, various and innumerable Idolatry, which completely strikes against the Commandment of the Lord and our Savior. This consists in a certain service rendered not to the Creator, but to the Creature, whether it be visible or invisible, bodily or spiritual, rational or irrational, whether by common nature or some art built up under the Name of Christ, or of the male and female Saints, of Relics, and of Powers alike. By these things, the same [creature] is openly served with faith, with hope, with works, with prayers, with pilgrimages, with alms, and with expensive ceremonies. Indeed, the Creature is honored and worshiped by them in various other ways, such as their songs of praise, eulogies, ceremonies, Mass-services, Vespers, the Praise, holy evenings, holy days, and finally the seeking of grace—which nonetheless is to be found essentially in God alone and in our Savior in view of his merits, and can be obtained by man through the Holy Spirit through Faith alone. And truly, the only cause of all Idolatry is located primarily in this: that one holds a false understanding of grace, of truth, of divine authority, of worship, and of mediation; and having taken these away from God, one transfers and appropriates them to his [the Antichrist's] validated ceremonies, the works of his hands, the Saints, and Purgatory. This iniquity of the False-Christ <note>original: "Leuge-Christus"</note> so directly strikes against the principal article of the Christian Faith that the first Commandment of the Law clearly forbids it. Likewise, from a disordered love for the world and the Antichrist, all evils and mistakes of the Church flow forth, such as those of her Leaders, Ministers, and Officials, who all together sin thereby without any punishment.

# General Memorial

<margin>3. Establishing the merit of works.</margin>
*False religions, rules, and ministries in the Church to acquire hope. For example, some people believe that if they devoutly hear Mass, use the Sacraments, or go to confession (though rarely truly contrite) and make satisfaction through fasting and emptying their purse, or if they have been or are a member of the Roman Church, or if they have given or surrendered themselves to a Rule or the cowl <note>original: "cappa" — the monastic habit or hood, representing entry into a religious order</note>, they claim against all truth that they must be saved. And this iniquity of the Antichrist is directly against the eighth article of the Creed: I believe in the Holy Spirit.*

<column-break/>

Furthermore, the aforementioned [Antichrist] has invented various false forms of worship, "Church orders" as they call them, and monasteries, pretending that one can obtain some hope of grace through them. Thus, he maintains and holds against all truth that everything rightly belongs to those who merely hear the Mass frequently and attentively, use the other Sacraments likewise, and especially repeat confession many times without, however, mixing any humility with it; making amends for evil with fasting and the emptying of the purse <note>original: "leeg-maken vande berus" — a reference to paying for indulgences or making mandatory donations to the church</note>; those who have been, or still are, Roman-minded and good churchmen, and have dedicated and willingly given themselves to the cowl or some Order, as they say. # Regarding the Events of the Waldensian Churches.

*...some up to the neck, others up to the waist, others only by a finger; and they say that sometimes they sit and eat at a table and have a banquet, especially when it is the Feast of All Souls <note>A day of prayer for the dead, observed on November 2nd</note>, when the people offer generously to the Priests upon their graves. And they say that sometimes they gather the crumbs under the tables of the rich. Because of all these things and many other lies, greed and simony <term>the buying or selling of sacred things or church offices</term> have increased and spread; and cloisters have been raised, and sumptuous temples built and enlarged, and they have multiplied altars beyond measure, along with an uncountable multitude of Monks and Canons; and they have meddled in other things which have given cause for expansion and indulgence, and they have held the Word of God in contempt. And the people are much deceived and cheated in their souls and their substance; they make them hope in uncertain things, and the faithful are hidden: and when they do not wish to teach this said Purgatory as an article of Faith, they are cruelly condemned to death and martyred. Therefore we are to speak of this Purgatory, and make known our opinion concerning it. We say first, that the souls of those to be saved must finally be purged of all their impurities according to the ordinance of God, as is manifest in Revelation 21 <note>original: "Apocalyps 21"</note>. Nothing that does anything abominable or a lie shall enter therein. We submit that Faith and Scripture show us many and diverse ways of purging by which those living in the present life are purged of all their sins, etc. But Saint Peter demonstrates in Acts 15 <note>original: "Act. 15"</note> that hearts are purifi-*

<column-break/>

up to the neck, others up to the waist in the aforementioned hellish forecourt <note>A vivid description of Purgatory as a place of physical torment</note>, and some suffer pain only in a finger: yet in such a way that they occasionally, and especially on All Souls' Day—when all the people are accustomed to offer very generously to the Priests <note>original: "Papen"</note> upon their graves—sit together at a table, eat a little, and make merry. Yes, others have gone so far as to say that they sometimes make them crawl under the tables of the rich to gather the crumbs there. But however they may differ in this, it all comes down to the same thing: that these lies and various others have advanced and multiplied greed and Simony <term>the corrupt practice of selling spiritual favors or church positions</term> to such an extent, raised up so many Monasteries, and founded and expanded so many costly and proud Churches; meanwhile an innumerable number of Monks and Canons or Prebendaries <note>original: "Stift-heeren," referring to members of a religious community</note> have devised other methods in turn, by which they would supposedly unbind and release those suffering souls. Through this, God's Word is also sufficiently mocked, and the poor people are most shamefully ensnared and deceived regarding both soul and money, being commanded by them to hope in something uncertain. Even the believers themselves are snatched away by this, because they—not wishing to teach the aforementioned Purgatory as an article of Faith—are for that very reason most cruelly condemned to death and most murderously mistreated. It will then also be worth the effort for us to speak a little of the same and express our feeling regarding it. To come to the point, we freely acknowledge that every soul that shall be saved must, according to God's command, once be unburdened and cleansed of all its impurities, as can be seen to some extent in the 21st chapter <note>The Dutch text mistakenly says "12. To wit, St. Peter clearly points this out to us in Acts, in the 15th chapter <margin>But such [purification] as happens through Faith.</margin>

...through Faith, and that Faith is sufficient to purge evil, without any other addition from outside. Just as it is manifest from the thief standing on the right <note>The "Penitent Thief" crucified alongside Jesus</note>, who, believing and quickly recognizing his sins, was made worthy of Paradise. Another way of purging the Bride of Christ through repentance is touched upon in Isaiah, in which place the Lord says: Wash yourselves and be clean, remove the evil of your thoughts from my eyes, and rest yourselves from acting perversely. It follows: Your sins shall be made white like snow; though they be like varnish <note>original: "verniz"; likely referring to a bright red or crimson dye</note>, they shall be like white wool. In which place the Lord shows himself to the truly penitent, according to the manner explained, that those who have sinned shall be made white as snow. Another way of purging sins is touched upon in Saint Matthew 3. In which place it says: The winnowing fan <term>a tool used to toss grain into the air so the wind blows the lighter chaff away</term> which is in his hand, he will clean his threshing floor, and gather the wheat into his granary. Which word Chrysostom <note>John Chrysostom (c. 347–407), an influential Early Church Father</note> explains as the threshing floor of the present Church, and of the fire of tribulations, but not only does the Lord cleanse his threshing floor through tribulations, but he cleanses for himself his Bride, even in this life. Just as Saint Paul says: Christ loved the Church, and gave himself for her, that he might sanctify her, cleansing her with the washing of water in the word of life, that he himself might present to himself a glorious Church, not having spot nor wrinkle nor any thing of this kind, but that she should be holy and without blemish. Whence the Apostle shows that Christ loved the Church so greatly that he did not wish to cleanse her with any other washing, but with his own blood, and not as if it were insufficient, but so that no impurity should remain:

<column-break/>

<margin>2. Through repentance.</margin>
*the hearts*, he says, *are sufficiently cleansed through Faith, and Faith alone is powerful enough to bring about the purification of sin without any external help.* This was evident in the thief (or murderer) who was crucified at the right hand of our Savior, since through bare faith and a proper confession of all his crimes he was deemed worthy of heaven. Again, we see in the Prophet Isaiah that the Bride of Christ <note>A common metaphor for the Church</note> can be washed in another way through repentance, where God the Lord is introduced speaking thus: *wash yourselves, cleanse yourselves, put away the wickedness of your thoughts from before my eyes, stop committing all evil:* and then a little further; *though your sins were as red as scarlet, they shall become as white as newly fallen snow; though they were as varnish (or crimson), they shall become as pure as fine wool.* And truly the Lord himself shows in that place to all true penitents, as we have mentioned here before, that such sinners shall surpass the white snow in beauty. Furthermore, we also see a third way of sin-washing in Saint Matthew in the 3rd Chapter, which mentions the same in this sense: *he has his winnowing fan in his hand, he will also thoroughly clean his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his barns, etc.* words which Saint Chrysostom has explained very well regarding the threshing floor of the present church and the fire of her visitations <note>referring to trials or persecutions</note>. But finally, the Lord Jesus is not even satisfied with this, unless he also cleanses his Bride in this life through himself, as Saint Paul somewhere teaches: *Christ*, he says, *has loved the Church and has given himself for her sake, that he might sanctify her to his glory, having washed her with the water-bath through the word of life, and she might thus subsequently become a glorious Church, that is, without spot, or wrinkle or any such thing, in a word, holy and blameless.* For the Apostle there clearly indicates that our Savior has loved his Church so much that he wished to wash her in no other bath than that of his own blood; not so much because the first was inadequate—

<margin>3. Through Tribulations.</margin>
<margin>4. Through the blood of Christ.</margin>

We finally assert that it is a most certain thing that each one should live in the present life in such a way that he needs no further purgation afterward. *For it is better to do good in the present life than to hope for uncertain help afterward. And a more secure life is that the good which someone hopes to be done by others after his death, he does for himself while he still lives; as it is a more blessed thing to depart as a free man than to seek liberty after being in bonds.*

These things having been set forth, we say that it is not expressly found in the Holy Scriptures of the Law of God, nor in the Holy Doctors <note>The "Church Fathers," early influential Christian theologians</note> founded upon the same, and not evasively—since no agreeable opinion is seen to be brought forth—that the faithful should be constrained by necessity to believe, nor hold, nor publicly confess as an article of Faith, that there is such a place as Purgatory after this life for sins, to which after Christ’s ascension to Heaven, the souls—especially of those who are to be saved—not having satisfied [for sins] in this life...

<column-break/>

...would be, especially since the smallest impurity would not be left in them; as he has clothed her with such glory that she is *without spot, or wrinkle, or anything of the sort, in a word, holy and blameless.* <note>original Dutch: "sonder vlak, of rimpel..."</note> This testimony of the washing of Christ's Bride in his own blood has not only echoed over the whole earth, but has even penetrated into Heaven, through those who have obtained that same actual purity there, as is witnessed somewhere in the Revelation: *these are they who have come out of the great tribulation, who have whitened and washed their garments in the Blood of the Lamb and therefore stand before the throne of the Lamb to serve the same.* Consequently, it can now be inferred from this that Faith and God’s Holy Word teach very clearly that the Believers, who are still traveling in this life, are also presently and completely cleansed of all their sins.

<margin>No remedy after death.</margin>
But we furthermore set this forth as an unquestionable matter: that everyone can conduct themselves so well in this present life that they need not expect the slightest purging afterward. And truly, it is far better to work for good during this life than to hope for an uncertain and hopeless aid afterward. It is likewise much more certain that one does that good oneself during one's life, which one hopes will be done by others after one's death. Not to mention that it is much more blessed to go hence in freedom than to seek the same after being in bonds.

<margin>Purgatory has no foundation either in the Holy Scriptures or in the ancient Teachers.</margin>
But above all that has been stated, we also say this openly: that in the Holy Scriptures of the divine Law, or those of the Holy Teachers founded upon them without deviation, there is not an express passage to be found from which it can in any way be drawn that the Believers are bound to believe unanimously, and to confess openly as a fundamental part of the Faith, that such a place or Purgatory <note>original: "Vage-vier"</note> is prepared after this life for sins, into which, immediately after the Ascension of our Savior <term>Salig-maker</term>, all souls—but especially those who look forward to eternal joys—still found <insert>something [to be satisfied]</insert> in this life...

### CHAPTER XVI.

#### Concerning the thirteenth Sample of the Waldensian Doctrine regarding the *Invocation of the Saints*, contained in a Writing named *The Invocation of the Saints* <note>original: "l'Invocation de li Sant"</note>, found in the aforementioned ancient manuscript from the year 1120.

<margin>
1. Reasons against it.
</margin>

*Now we must speak of the invocation of the Saints, which the Masters <note>The "Masters" refers to the established church leadership criticized by the Waldensians.</note>, adding to their own doctrines, preach and promote with great diligence, publishing it as an article of Faith; saying that the Saints existing in the celestial Fatherland are to be prayed to by us who are living, in the manner that the Priests and other commoners usually use by their instruction, enjoining upon themselves and others things for the aid of invocation. By which invocation, authorization, and magnification, the people are seen to perceive this carnally and errantly: believing that just as it is done before an earthly King who is angry, where others (who are not angry) intercede for someone, mitigating his anger before him, even so the people estimate it to be done before God—that the Saints, turning toward the sinner, mitigate His anger.*

*And this is seen to be not worthy of belief, as it would seem there is no true conformity of the will of the Saints with the will of God: for at that point—*

<column-break/>

WE have now further to speak of the *Worship of the Saints* here, which all Preaching Friars <term>Preaching Friars: specifically the Dominican Order, known for their public sermons</term> and their Church-wardens, or Suffragans <term>Suffragan: an assistant bishop or a high-ranking ecclesiastical official</term>, everywhere teach as a principal part of the Faith, impressing it upon the people and diligently exalting it; saying that the Saints, who have already arrived in the Heavenly Fatherland, must be worshipped according to the common use of the Priests, just as the same is followed with great zeal by the common people according to their instruction, accompanied by many other additions for enlightenment. And truly, regarding this so-strengthened and glorious Service of Saints, it seems nevertheless that the common folk <note>original: "’t grauwe", referring to the uneducated masses</note> hold very carnal and doubtful feelings; believing namely, and holding for certain, that it happens there just as with earthly kings, who, when ignited with righteous wrath against someone, are softened and persuaded to drop it through the intervention of beloved and mediating favorites; and that in like manner, I say, the Saints come to lay down God's wrath through their intercession on behalf of sinners.

Which, however, when well-considered, cannot be too well believed, because in that case, there would first be no true harmony between the will of God and that of the Saints—

### Y 3
<meta>catchword: can</meta>

*...to whom God would be indignant, for it would not seem right that they themselves would be without him.* <note>original: "alqual Dio sendegnaria non seria vist que illi meseime seirè sensa luy."</note>

*Secondly, through this glorification and invocation of the Saints, the people fall into Idolatry, placing more trust in one of the Saints than in God, and serving them more affectionately than the only God, demonstrating this by their deeds: by the adornment of more precious altars, by more resonant bells, and the multiplication of candles, and other ceremonies. By which things it appears to the simple folk that these [Saints] are more merciful than God, and that those whom He Himself has condemned, they themselves might still deliver from damnation through their prayers. By which thing, in addition to this, the simple learn that the Saints desire gifts, offerings, and personal praises, and that they intercede mostly for those who give them incense, offerings, and other praises—all of which things are to be avoided and loathed with great diligence. Therefore we end our speaking of this invocation of the Saints, and declare our intention concerning it.*

*Firstly, and before all things, we maintain that the name of this Invocation and the act of Invoking is the same: the desire of the whole mind and the whole soul that sends its voice in prayer to the only God. We maintain, secondly, that the man Christ is the mediator between God and men, and the Advocate before the Father, and the one who satisfies for our sins. Approaching God for Himself, and living always to pray for us. No one comes to the Father except through Him. And whatever you shall ask of the Father in my name, I will do it. He who gives to all abundantly and does not reproach. And He is the Advocate before the Father, and the forgiver of our sins.*
